Each `BASNonModelProposalInput` binds exactly one canonical packet digest and
one contained `BASNonModelProposalPlan`; it never references the model-only
`BASExecutionPlan` ABI. It cannot render or retain a prompt, tokenizer, token
IDs, Provider reference or step, model identity/profile, or Provider-private
KV. `classicML` means certified bounded non-open-generative inference only.
The world-model-plus-search composite preserves two causal producer edges:
bounded inference first emits prediction evidence, then search consumes that
evidence and emits the selected plan. Reopen proves exactly two causal edges:
`boundedInferenceReceiptArtifactID -> predictionEvidenceArtifactID` and
`predictionEvidenceArtifactID -> searchPlanArtifactID`; the search plan's
exact ordered parent is the same prediction evidence. Neither producer becomes
a Provider, parallel compiler, or implicit model execution plan.

The contained non-model ABI is closed rather than caller-selectable:

| candidate kind | exact non-model input profile |
|---|---|
| `rule` | `policyState` |
| `search` | `constraintGraph` |
| `classicML` | `tensorState` |
| `human` | `structuredPacketDirect` |
| `tool` | `programIR` |

`BASNonModelProposalPlan.init`, its exact-key decoder, and the sole W4 plan
admission validator all reject a candidate/proof mismatch. The validator
reopens every plan Artifact, computes
`SHA256("qinao.nonmodel-proposal-plan.v1" || candidateKind || canonicalProof ||
algorithmOrCapabilityArtifactID || boundedResourcePolicyArtifactID ||
expectedOutputSchemaArtifactID || orderedCausalParentArtifactIDs)`, and requires
byte equality with `planDigest`; no caller-supplied digest is trusted. For the
world-model/search case it additionally reopens the bounded-inference
completion receipt and prediction Artifact, proves the first edge, reopens the
search completion and selected-plan Artifact, proves the second edge, and
requires the selected search-plan digest to equal `planDigest` with the
prediction evidence as its one exact ordered parent. Omitted, reordered,
duplicated, foreign-Attempt, foreign-packet, foreign-profile or merely
same-content causal IDs fail closed. `BASNonModelProposalInput.init` then binds
that admitted plan to the exact packet digest and table profile.
The incumbent compiler's store-aware
`BASContextCompiler.makeNonModelMaterialization(packet:selectedPlanArtifactID:capabilityProfile:artifactStore:)`
and
`BASContextCompiler.makeModelMaterialization(packet:selectedExecutionPlanArtifactID:mechanismProof:capabilityProfile:compiledContext:artifactStore:)`
are the sole W4 compiler-extension factories accepted by execution. The model factory reopens
`selectedExecutionPlanArtifactID` as the one existing `BASExecutionPlan`,
requires its current execution binding to select candidate `.model`, the same
proof/profile and exact packet, and validates the incumbent
`BASExactCompiledContext.descriptor` without extending that runtime-only type:
its `semanticSnapshotArtifactID`, `stateMarketSelectionArtifactID`, and
`executionBindingArtifactID` must reopen to the packet snapshot, the exact
market selection and that selected plan/binding, while its incumbent
`budgetReceipt` matches the same binding and packet budget. The factory then
rechecks the outer case and canonical token/span/descriptor fingerprint. A
foreign plan, descriptor, packet, proof, profile or budget receipt fails; a
directly formed runtime enum value is inert and ineligible. The non-model
factory symmetrically reopens the selected plan, mechanism certification,
algorithm/capability, resource policy, output schema and ordered causal
parents, recomputes `planDigest`, validates the exact input-profile row and
packet/profile binding, and only then chooses the matching outer enum case.
Neither pure initialization nor decode can mint an admitted materialization.

`BASProposalMechanismEvidence` is a contained value inside the existing proof
wire, not an independently governed payload, ordinary-put body, schema-registry
row, store, producer, or owner. Reopen `certificationReceiptArtifactID` as the
incumbent `BASArtifactAttestationPayload`; its target is
`mechanismArtifactID`, and its signed-statement preimage binds the proof kind
plus the first nine evidence fields from `mechanismArtifactID` through
`resourceClosureRoot`. It excludes `certificationReceiptArtifactID` itself to
avoid a content-addressed self-reference; the downstream proof/plan canonical
digest binds all ten fields. Capability-profile compatibility remains a
separate pure admission check and is not duplicated into the certification.
The attestation purpose is exactly
`qinao.proposal-mechanism-certification.v1`; its incumbent signature, key,
custody, logical-time, and policy-currentness validation must succeed before
the contained evidence can be admitted. The work-completion or producer-use
receipt remains a separate branch input and is never replaced by this
certification.
`BASProposalMechanismProof` uses one explicit `kind/evidence` strict decoder
with an exact key set; synthesized enum Codable is forbidden.
Reopened mechanism evidence binds `mechanismArtifactID`, `mechanismID`,
`mechanismVersion`, `codeOrModelDigest`, `determinismClass`,
`usesLanguageInference`, `usesLearnedInference`, `mayOpenGenerate`,
`resourceClosureRoot`, and `certificationReceiptArtifactID`; the one pure
admission validator checks the proof kind and selected capability profile
against those facts. Ordinary construction, strict decode, plan admission,
grounding, and superstep admission all reuse that validator rather than
trusting an enum tag.

The candidate-to-mechanism-proof mapping is exact and uses only the canonical
six candidate kinds:

| candidate kind | admitted mechanism proofs |
|---|---|
| `rule` | `deterministic` |
| `search` | `deterministic,boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch` |
| `classicML` | `boundedNonLanguageLearned,boundedLanguageLearned` |
| `human` | `structuredHuman,languageHuman` |
| `tool` | `structuredTool,languageTool,deterministicTool` |
| `model` | `openGenerativeProvider` |

The proof tag is insufficient by itself. The shared pure validator also
requires this exact contained-evidence truth table before any profile check:

| mechanism proof | determinismClass | usesLanguageInference | usesLearnedInference | mayOpenGenerate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deterministic` | `deterministic` | `false` | `false` | `false` |
| `deterministicTool` | `deterministic` | `false` | `false` | `false` |
| `boundedNonLanguageLearned` | `boundedNondeterministic` | `false` | `true` | `false` |
| `boundedLanguageLearned` | `boundedNondeterministic` | `true` | `true` | `false` |
| `boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch` | `boundedNondeterministic` | `false` | `true` | `false` |
| `structuredHuman` | `externallySupplied` | `false` | `false` | `false` |
| `languageHuman` | `externallySupplied` | `true` | `false` | `false` |
| `structuredTool` | `externallySupplied` | `false` | `false` | `false` |
| `languageTool` | `externallySupplied` | `true` | `false` | `false` |
| `openGenerativeProvider` | `providerOpaque` | `true` | `true` | `true` |

For the composite row the facts come from
`BASWorldModelSearchCausalProof.mechanismEvidence`. A mismatch between tag and
any fact fails even under `fullProvider`; the selected profile then subtracts
proof kinds through the next table. Thus a forged structured tag cannot hide a
language, learned or open-generative mechanism. Reopening and validating the
digest-bound incumbent attestation is a prerequisite to this pure validation,
and the same admitted mechanism certification may be reused across profiles;
Attempt/profile compatibility is checked separately at admission.

| capability profile | admitted mechanism proofs |
|---|---|
| fullProvider | `deterministic,boundedNonLanguageLearned,boundedLanguageLearned,structuredHuman,languageHuman,structuredTool,languageTool,deterministicTool,openGenerativeProvider,boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch` |
| noGenerativeProvider | `deterministic,boundedNonLanguageLearned,boundedLanguageLearned,structuredHuman,languageHuman,structuredTool,languageTool,deterministicTool,boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch` |
| noLanguageInference | `deterministic,boundedNonLanguageLearned,structuredHuman,structuredTool,deterministicTool,boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch` |
| noLearnedInference | `deterministic,structuredHuman,structuredTool,deterministicTool` |

The exact capability matrix is:

| profile | candidate kinds | grounding branches | open-language availability |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fullProvider` | `rule,search,classicML,human,tool,model` | `model,boundedInference,deterministic,humanOrTool,notRequired` | `availableOrTypedUnavailable` |
| `noGenerativeProvider` | `rule,search,classicML,human,tool` | `boundedInference,deterministic,humanOrTool,notRequired` | `externalProducerRequired` |
| `noLanguageInference` | rule,search,classicML,human,tool | `boundedInference,deterministic,humanOrTool,notRequired` | `externalProducerRequired` |
| `noLearnedInference` | `rule,search,human,tool` | `deterministic,humanOrTool,notRequired` | `externalProducerRequired` |

The selected `BASCapabilityExecutionProfile` is frozen for the complete
Attempt; same-Attempt profile replacement is forbidden. A capability change
returns typed unavailable or starts a new Attempt.
`waitingForModel` is legal only under `fullProvider` and only while an admitted
recoverable model plan remains current.

Superstep 7 applies the same candidate/mechanism proof closure at construction
and strict decode:

| capability profile | legal superstep-7 work and proof |
|---|---|
| fullProvider | `providerPrefillDecode:openGenerativeProvider;boundedInference:boundedNonLanguageLearned,boundedLanguageLearned,boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch;deterministicProposal:deterministic;humanOrTool:structuredHuman,languageHuman,structuredTool,languageTool,deterministicTool;noWork:notRequired` |
| noGenerativeProvider | `boundedInference:boundedNonLanguageLearned,boundedLanguageLearned,boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch;deterministicProposal:deterministic;humanOrTool:structuredHuman,languageHuman,structuredTool,languageTool,deterministicTool;noWork:notRequired` |
| noLanguageInference | `boundedInference:boundedNonLanguageLearned,boundedNonLanguageWorldModelSearch;deterministicProposal:deterministic;humanOrTool:structuredHuman,structuredTool,deterministicTool;noWork:notRequired` |
| noLearnedInference | `deterministicProposal:deterministic;humanOrTool:structuredHuman,structuredTool,deterministicTool;noWork:notRequired` |

A noWork observation is admitted only after reopening the exact current
notRequired disposition receipt and proving it is neither unavailable nor
coverageDeficit.
Every superstep-7 provider or non-provider work receipt is reopened and must
match the outer TurnOperation, Attempt, candidate kind, mechanism proof,
Context Packet digest, and capability profile.
`BASSuperstepSevenExecutionKind` also uses an explicit strict tagged decoder;
synthesized enum Codable cannot bypass profile/work validation.

Superstep 7 has two deliberately separate validation stages. The public
initializers and exact-key decoders call only the package-visible pure
`BASSuperstepSevenObservationReceipt.validateProfileWorkCompatibility`; a
successfully decoded value is inert and ineligible for execution. The existing
`runtime.semantic-dag` owner then exposes the one package function
`BASSemanticTurnDAG.admitSuperstepSevenObservation(decoded:artifactStore:expectedTurnOperationRef:expectedAttemptRefArtifactID:expectedStructuredContextPacketDigest:expectedCapabilityProfile:) async throws`.
It receives the already-opened incumbent `BASArtifactStorePort` and does not
create a store, writer, registry row, scheduler or execution authority.

That store-aware admission first requires the outer operation, Attempt,
canonical packet digest and Attempt-frozen profile to equal the expected
values, then reopens every contained mechanism certification and reruns the
shared tag/facts/candidate/profile validator. For `providerPrefillDecode` it
reopens `providerExecutionRef` and `workReceiptArtifactID` as the incumbent
Provider execution and terminal-work wrappers and requires both to match the
same outer operation, Attempt, packet, model candidate, open-generative proof,
profile and selected model plan. For each non-provider case it reopens the
actual bounded-inference, deterministic-proposal or authenticated human/tool
completion wrapper at `workReceiptArtifactID` and requires its operation,
Attempt, packet, candidate, proof, profile, output and resource closure to
match the outer receipt; a generic attestation is not work completion. For
`noWork` it reopens the exact current
`BASR5ProducerAvailabilityReceipt` named by
`notRequiredDispositionReceiptArtifactID`, matches the same operation,
Attempt, packet/snapshot epoch and profile, and accepts only
`.notRequired`; `.unavailable`, `.coverageDeficit`, a stale receipt or an open
obligation fails. The function returns the admitted receipt only after all
reopens; strict decoding alone can never advance the superstep.

R4 and R5 must close availability explicitly rather than treating absence as
work or omission:

| phase | required receipt | forbidden fallback |
|---|---|---|
| `R4 dense_semantic` | `BASR4DenseLaneAvailabilityReceipt` | `silentRunOrSilentSkip` |
| `R5 dedupe_fusion_bounded_grounding_proposal` | `BASR5ProducerAvailabilityReceipt` | `unavailableAsNotRequiredOrCrossBranch` |

R4 and R5 cannot advance until their exact current disposition receipt is durably committed and reopened.
Each disposition carries the exact evidence Artifact for available execution/
profile, unavailable reason/currentness, frozen omission, or open coverage
obligation respectively. `notRequired` is legal only after complete
required coverage is proven; it cannot hide a `coverageDeficit` or substitute
for `unavailable`.

State Market keeps exactly the same seven fields. Before candidate election,
`State Market.tokenCost = BASModelNeutralMarketCost.conservativeTokenCost`.
The `BASSemanticStateMarket` factory reopens the exact
`BASStructuredContextPacket` and its canonical resource inventory, recomputes
`canonicalByteCount`, `canonicalSectionCount`, and `resourceUnitCount`, and
rejects caller-supplied basis drift; direct construction is package-private and
decoded values remain ineligible until the same semantic validator succeeds.
The factory enumerates every explicit packet reference into the closed
`artifact`, `evidenceSpan`, `outputSchema`, `toolOrCapability`, or `attachment`
`BASModelNeutralResourceInventoryRow` kind. It canonical-sorts unique rows by
`(resourceKind.rawValue, canonicalResourceID UTF-8, contentDigest)` and rejects
an exact duplicate tuple, the same `(kind, ID)` with a different digest, an
omitted packet reference, a foreign row, a reordered row or a digest mismatch.
One exact resource shared by several packet sections appears once; a resource
whose monetary or execution cost is zero still contributes one unit.
`resourceUnitCount` must equal the unique canonical row count, and
`resourceInventoryDigest` must equal the domain-separated
`SHA256("qinao.model-neutral-resource-inventory.v1" || canonicalRows)`.
Reorder, duplicate, omit, shared-resource and foreign-digest mutation fixtures
all pass through this same factory rather than a test-only calculator.
That conservative cost is derived only from canonical byte, section, and
resource units under `qinao.market-token-units.v1` as one unit per byte plus
eight units per section plus thirty-two units per resource. Every multiply/add
is checked and overflow fails closed; it has no model or tokenizer dependency.
`BASProviderExactAccounting` is emitted only after a
`model` election and is Provider-exact operational evidence; its actual token
counts cannot feed eligibility, ranking, the frozen market, or a re-election.

Observable superstep 7 remains the existing compatibility name **Prefill and
Decode** and ordinal `7`; it does not create an eleventh superstep. Its receipt
records the branch's real work. Only `providerPrefillDecode` carries a
`BASSuperstepSevenProviderWork` whose `providerExecutionRef` is the sole
`BASProviderExecutionRef`; bounded inference, deterministic proposal,
human/tool work, and typed no-work do not impersonate Provider execution and
are not collapsed into `noWork`.

The exact owner/path/wave placement is closed:

| Slice | Existing owner | Exact production path and permitted first wire |
|---|---|---|
| W1 contract | `state.snapshot-contracts` | `BehavioralAISubstrate/Sources/BASRuntimeCore/BASSemanticStateLakeContracts.swift` declares the closed candidate-kind/profile, contained mechanism evidence and typed proof/world-search causal proof, structured Proposal, canonical Context Packet, typed proposal/phase availability, R4/R5 receipt, contained five-kind model-neutral resource row, eight-field model-neutral market-cost basis, and strict tagged grounding values in its already-approved non-empty M first wire; `BASMemory/BASAgentFabricEnums.swift` atomically replaces the delegation-origin/proposal lineage wire under the same owner; neither path adds engine behavior. |
| W1 Automation contract | `runtime.semantic-dag` | `BehavioralAISubstrate/Sources/BASRuntimeCore/BASSemanticTurnDAG.swift` extends the signed structured-definition intake, frozen-slot values, typed Provider/non-Provider/no-work evidence, and strict branch-exact superstep-7 observation value only; no scheduler, producer, activation, or write behavior. |

#### B. Dynamic DAG, mission graph, rebase, checkpoint, and recovery closure

```text
BASSemanticTurnEdge = {fromSlotID,toSlotID,dependencyRole,consumerInputSlotContractDigest}
dependencyRole = dataConsumption|controlBarrier|authorization|budget|snapshot|verification|effectPredecessor|publicationPredecessor
BASSemanticTurnEdgeBinding = {edgeID,predecessorTerminalReceiptArtifactID,predecessorOutputArtifactID,consumerInputSlotID,consumerBindingArtifactID,attemptID,generation,epoch}
optional-slot contract = BASDelegationSlotContract
```

`BASSemanticTurnEdge` and `BASDelegationSlotContract` are static topology;
`BASSemanticTurnEdgeBinding` and `BASDelegationSlotClosure` are the governed
Attempt-bound bindings/closures; static topology never embeds dynamic receipt IDs.
Every node binds role, purpose, input/output schemas, capability ceiling,
budget/deadline ceiling and completion predicate. Every edge binds predecessor
receipt, consumed Artifact/output, destination input slot, dependency role and
current binding/epoch identity. Each optional slot closes exactly once as
`boundTerminal`, `provedUnused`, or `rejectedBeforeAllocation`; a frozenSlot
cannot be appended, widened or rebound. An alternative names a finite ordered
choice set and one selection receipt. A delegation is depth one and refers to
one predeclared slot. A join freezes source order, required/optional membership,
correlation/common-mode classes, conflict/missing-child behavior and terminal
Attempt refs. Runtime may fill, skip, order or parallelize the frozen graph but
cannot create a node, role, descendant, capability or authority.

The same owner first-governs one immutable mission graph value with the exact
hierarchy `Mission → Objective → WorkUnit → Attempt → SolutionArtifact`.
Every node has a stable key, parent key, ordered child keys, typed completion
predicate and status; every Attempt and SolutionArtifact references its
WorkUnit and exact DAG root. K3 owns the one active mission/task-graph root CAS
and successor reference. The graph value owns no scheduler or mutable truth.

An atomic context rebase keeps one visible Workspace while rotating its active
Attempt. The only legal sequence is:

```text
ACTIVE(n)
→ rebase_requested at a terminal-safe boundary
→ ContextContinuityManifest + coverage + predecessor terminal proof
→ K3 rebase_pending with inherited budget/round/visited-state proof
→ K4 inactive successor grant reservation
→ K3 active-head CAS and BASAttemptRebaseReceipt
→ K4 activation: usable | activationPending | terminalDenied
```

The successor grant is attenuated and inactive until the active-head CAS wins.
A pre-CAS crash resubmits only the byte-identical reservation/CAS request. A
post-CAS crash reopens the winning receipt and activates the same reservation.
An activation-unknown result stays pending; denial never rolls the head back.
No state permits two active Attempts or two usable grants. Provider/KV/cache/
session/call identities never cross the rebase.

`boundaryUninterrupted` additionally proves that no suspension, expiration
handoff, cancellation/interruption, actor/task replacement, or execution-

| same-boot Provider `Q!=nil`, `O/S=nil`, the original owner remains live, but bound currentness/deadline fails or the exact invocation is no longer demonstrably live, and an exact same-operation cancellation/quiescence/query/terminal protocol exists | `reconcileOnly` | use only that existing invocation's policy-permitted cancellation, quiescence, query, or terminalization path; mint no call permit, adopt no now-ineligible output, and restore no `CP` |
| the same claimed, same-boot, still-live-owner shape has no exact same-operation cancellation/quiescence/query/terminal protocol | `quarantined` | request no replacement call and infer no terminal fact; retain the unresolved identity for incident/user policy |
| same-boot AFM `Q!=nil`, `O/S=nil`, owner lost, and exact terminal/cancellation-quiescence or authenticated same-operation recovery evidence exists | `reconcileOnly` | seal/query/reconcile that operation only; never create a generation permit or restore `CP` in another process |
| isolated/remote, including system-managed remote, `Q!=nil`, `O/S=nil`, owner lost, and authenticated same-operation recovery evidence exists | `reconcileOnly` | query/reconcile that operation only; never create a generation permit or restore `CP` in another process |
| same-boot AFM or any isolated/remote/system-managed-remote `Q!=nil`, `O/S=nil`, owner lost, and no exact terminal/quiescence or authenticated same-operation recovery evidence exists | `quarantined` | do not infer silence from App death; retain unresolved truth and require a separately confirmed independent WorkUnit for later work |
| `O!=nil`, `S=nil`, observation origin is `immediateReturn`, observation boot equals claim/arm boot, and current same-boot epochs hold | `reconcileOnly` | reopen the exact observation/attestation and perform only the existing K3 seal CAS; zero Provider calls |
| `O!=nil`, `S=nil`, origin is `authenticatedQueryRecovery`, its attestation binds the original isolated/remote tuple plus current recovery boot, and current generation/policy/deletion/revocation epochs hold | `reconcileOnly` | perform only the existing cross-boot query-recovery seal exception; mint no permit and rewrite no historical boot |
| `O!=nil`, `S=nil`, origin and attestation shape are otherwise valid, but current generation/policy/deletion/revocation epochs fail | `quarantined` | retain only policy-permitted audit/erasure evidence; adopt no proposal/result, perform no terminal seal under stale authority, and issue no Provider call |
| `O!=nil`, `S=nil`, but an `immediateReturn` observation crosses boot or either origin/attestation shape is invalid | `quarantined` | no terminal mutation or adoption |
| `S` is terminal, current boot still matches, and no later visibility/publication/effect boundary is open | `terminal` | continue deterministic gates or become same-boot strict-rebase eligible |
| `S` is terminal from an earlier boot and the complete WorkUnit, including publication/effect K3 closures, is already terminal | `terminalReadOnly` | restore the completed response/audit projection only; perform no K3 mutation |
| `S` is terminal from an earlier boot but downstream K3 work is unfinished | `quarantined` | do not mutate the old boot; await an explicitly confirmed independent WorkUnit |
| `P!=nil`, `Jr=nil`, no `D/K/B/X`, `sameLiveOwner` | `safePreclaim` | reserve only the same publication identity and continue its once-only path |
| `P!=nil`, `Jr=nil`, no `D/K/B/X`, same boot and exact original owner/epochs remain current, but the publication deadline expired | `closedUnused` | create no journal reserve or sink call; retain or erase the immutable prepared spool only through its existing Artifact retention/erasure owner |
| `P!=nil`, `Jr=nil`, no `D/K/B/X`, same boot and exact original owner remains live, but generation/policy/deletion/revocation currentness fails | `quarantined` | create no journal reserve or sink call; permit only the existing erasure/incident path and never adopt the prepared bytes under changed authority |
| `P!=nil`, `Jr=nil`, no `D/K/B/X`, same boot and the exact original owner is lost | `quarantined` | create no journal reserve or sink call; preserve only policy-permitted audit/erasure evidence and require a separately confirmed independent WorkUnit for later visible work |
| `P!=nil`, `Jr=nil`, no `D/K/B/X`, and the prepared publication belongs to an earlier boot | `staleBoot` | preserve it read-only, perform no old-boot close/reserve/sink mutation, and await a separately confirmed independent WorkUnit |
| `Jr!=nil`, `K` proved absent, no anchor request was ever issued or lost, no `B/X`, `sameLiveOwner` | `safePreclaim` | continue only that exact journal plus its unique first dormant permit/anchor sequence; no second publication identity |
| publication `Jr!=nil`, `K` proved absent after anchor submission/result/reply became uncertain, `Jf=nil`, `sameLiveOwner` | `reconcileOnly` | journal lookup/query-close only; never submit the anchor or invoke the sink |
| publication `Jr!=nil`, `K` proved absent, `Jf=nil`, the same-boot original owner remains live, but currentness/deadline fails | `reconcileOnly` | journal lookup/query-close only; never submit the anchor or invoke the sink |
| publication `Jr!=nil`, `Jf=nil`, and either its owner/boot was lost, `K/B` committed, or current `K/B` status remains unknown | `reconcileOnly` | journal lookup/finalize/close only; never invoke the sink |
| `Jf!=nil`, K3 publication close exists | `terminalReadOnly` | restore finalized bytes; execute no sink call, including after reboot |
| `Jf!=nil`, K3 publication close is absent, same boot/current owner permits closure | `reconcileOnly` | install only the existing K3 close from the exact finalization record; no sink call |
| `Jf!=nil`, K3 publication close is absent, same boot, but owner/current epochs do not permit closure | `quarantined` | retain the finalization for policy-permitted audit/erasure only; perform no K3 close or sink call |
| `Jf!=nil`, K3 publication close is absent after reboot | `quarantined` | keep the finalization auditable but perform no cross-boot K3 close |
| Zone-C pending, `K` proved absent, no anchor request was ever issued or lost, no `B/X`, `sameLiveOwner` | `safePreclaim` | continue only the same saga's unique first permit/anchor sequence, or close unused |
| Zone-C pending, `K` proved absent after anchor submission/result/reply became uncertain, `sameLiveOwner` | `reconcileOnly` | query-close/reconcile the same saga identity only; never submit the anchor or dispatch |
| Zone-C pending has `K` proved absent, the same-boot original owner remains live, but currentness/deadline fails | `reconcileOnly` | query-close/reconcile the same saga identity only; never submit the anchor or dispatch |
| terminal effect receipt is nil, and either the Zone-C owner/boot was lost, `K/B` committed, or current `K/B` status remains unknown | `reconcileOnly` | query/reconcile that exact saga; never redispatch |
| terminal effect receipt and its K3 seal/activation both exist | `terminalReadOnly` | reopen the completed result for read-only audit/projection; zero effect calls |
| terminal effect receipt exists but K3 seal/activation is absent, same boot/current owner permits closure | `reconcileOnly` | install only the existing K3 closure/activation from that receipt; zero effect calls |
| terminal effect receipt exists but K3 seal/activation is absent, same boot, and owner/current epochs do not permit closure | `quarantined` | retain only policy-permitted audit/erasure evidence; perform no K3 closure/activation or effect call |
| terminal effect receipt exists but K3 seal/activation is absent after reboot | `quarantined` | perform no cross-boot closure/activation; await operator/user recovery policy |

The rows are mutually exclusive after first partitioning by boundary kind and boot relation, then equality-checking presence, possible-start, terminal, owner liveness, currentness, observation origin, and closure presence; an anchor with `Q=nil` is still possible-start and is never conflated with an unanchored dormant permit. Provider recovery actions use the Provider rows under their own finite ordinals. The WorkUnit aggregate is deterministic across those independently classified boundaries: any `quarantined` class yields `quarantine`; otherwise any `reconcileOnly` yields `reconcileSameOperation`; otherwise a fully completed graph containing only `terminal/terminalReadOnly/closedUnused` yields `restoreCompleted`; otherwise any `staleBoot`, expired confirmation/user-presence, interrupted visible prefix, missing mandatory context, changed Provider/account/region/disclosure/cost/effect identity, or unfinished earlier-boot graph yields `awaitUser`; otherwise an unfinished same-boot graph with only `terminal/terminalReadOnly/closedUnused` predecessors creates or revalidates the exact strict rebase request and yields `rebuildAfterTerminal`; otherwise any `safePreclaim/liveSameBoundary/liveSameInvocation` yields `resumeSameAttempt`. Aggregate precedence resolves different boundaries, not overlapping predicates. A pending confirmation is restored as pending; it is never answered on the user's behalf. Two windows or recovery workers race through the same existing K3 CAS/claim and at most one wins.

W1 also declares strict-Codable
`BASAutomationCheckpointInstallRequest`,
`BASAutomationCheckpointInstallReceipt`,
`BASAutomationCheckpointReopenRequest`, and
`BASAutomationCheckpointReopenReceipt`. Each binds operation/run/version,
checkpoint and continuity-manifest Artifact IDs/digests, recovery-cursor
digest, expected K3 head/row version, current epoch vector, idempotency key,
exact `recovery72Hours` retention-admission receipt Artifact ID/digest,
committed head/new row version, trusted commit time and post-state root. The
checkpoint owns no copied expiry/minimum/maximum clock; it reopens the sole
retention decision. Both cursor and checkpoint use
the same tagged proof: latest budget-use receipt XOR K3 zero-use proof. Zero-
use is legal only before first spend; after spend only the exact latest receipt
is legal. Missing, both-present, stale or foreign proof rejects.

`ContinuationPolicy.validate(...)` is the sole semantic factory/reopen check
over trusted-now, interruption evidence, foreground/user presence, boundary
class and requested execution class. It rejects expired deadline or
`maximumInterruptionAgeMs`, `automaticWhenSafe` with a mutation-capable class
after possible-start/interruption, stale/foreign/replayed affirmative input,
and any policy widening. `confirmationAfterInterruption` requires an exact
one-use affirmative Input Event; `neverAutomatic` never mutates on relaunch.

`ContextContinuityManifest.validateReopenedLineage(...)` exact-compares the
manifest and cursor as the same TurnOperation, snapshot, graph, generation,
epoch, and Workspace lineage. It also compares active Attempt, mission/task
roots, current heads, source HWM and continuation-policy receipt. Checks that
need authoritative currentness live in this owner factory plus the incumbent
K3 reopen gate rather than permissive field initializers. Foreign splice,
mixed epoch, cross-Workspace and stale-head mutations all fail.

#### C. Causality and observable reasoning closure

Qinao keeps three non-interchangeable tracks. Execution dependency is an
Attempt-bound typed edge in `runtime.semantic-dag`. `ClaimSupportMap` is the
L10 `semantics.layercell` nested value in the one exact-output parent.
`WorldClaimSet` is the L4 `semantics.layercell` versioned relation value.
`ExplanationProjection` is the deterministic L12 projection; execution dependency
is never interchangeable with either semantic claim family, and the projection is referenced,
not re-owned, by `runtime.turn-operation`.

Every ClaimSupport evidence edge binds claim ID and exact final-spool UTF-8
span, normalized proposition digest, evidence Artifact and raw UTF-8 span,
transformation/verifier receipts, authority, epistemic state and one of
`supports`, `contradicts`, `insufficient`, `notApplicable`. Every material
claim has exactly one aggregate `supported`, `contradicted`, `conflicted`,
`insufficient` or `notApplicable` plus canonical edge IDs. Mixed support and
contradiction remains `conflicted`; score, majority and last writer cannot
erase it.

`WorldClaimSet` distinguishes temporal predecessor, co-occurrence, association
hypothesis, causal hypothesis, supported causal claim and refuted causal claim.
sequence and co-occurrence never establish world causation. Resolved causation
requires exact cause/effect propositions, scope/time, assumptions/confounders,
sources/provenance, qualified support/contradiction and independently governed
intervention, hold-fixed or counterfactual proof. Changes are predecessor-
linked versions, never in-place promotion.

The W6 retirement slice classifies persisted rows and all production
reachability through `BASKnowledgeGraphEventExtractor`, storage/preload,
builder/convenience and user-state reducers. The incumbent
`LegacyCausality.projectUntrustedAssociations` may downgrade old `.causes`
rows to historical/association-only or quarantine them; those rows cannot
reach L4 world claims, L5/L6 user state, exact release, or learning truth.
Projectors use a throwing sequence-bounded EventLog read and one K3 cursor/root
CAS; catch-to-empty and timestamp cursor advancement cannot commit.

`ExplanationProjection` derives disclosure-filtered bytes from the frozen
Attempt/DAG, exact spool, ClaimSupportMap, WorldClaimSet refs, owner receipts,
effect and publication outcomes. Identical roots replay byte-identically.
There is no second causal database, explanation ledger or projector manager.

Observable reasoning uses bounded typed work products, never raw CoT. The W1
`ConstraintLedger` binds variables/domains, hard and soft constraints,
ordering relations, unresolved clauses, every raw UTF-8 span, canonical AST,
normalized interpretation, source and epistemic modality. Candidate, critique,
uncertainty, counterexample, perspective, clarification and verification
artifacts bind exact parents and output schemas. A `VerifierClaimContract`
states exact subclaim, input/environment domain, accepted language, soundness,
coverage/completeness, blind spots, nondeterminism and version; a compiler,
unit test, SQL run or format check proves only its declared subclaim.

A cognitive parent earns process evidence only when committed before use and
an exact downstream-consumer receipt proves consumption. Post-hoc or unused
reasoning is `explanationOnly` and receives zero process reward and zero causal credit.
Used contributions are labeled exactly `directAttribution`,
`diagnosticAssociation`, `identifiedCausalEffect`, or `indeterminate`.
Correlation, replay/ablation or Shapley/COMA diagnostics cannot be relabeled as
identified causation without a randomized logged intervention or validated
supported causal model.

#### D. Provider-neutral context, grounding, API, and Core AI closure

W1 extends the existing model/profile and context-contract candidates. A
versioned `CertifiedContextGeometry` in the signed profile freezes exactly one
cap topology—`sharedTotal`, `splitInputOutput`, or `encoderOnly`—and one
accounting proof—`deterministicTokenSpans`, `opaqueRuntimeExactCount`, or
`certifiedConservativeUpperBound`. It binds material/remote cohort, tokenizer
or opaque-accounting contract, template/tool/schema, reasoning reserve,
ProcessorABI/StateABI/mask/position geometry, caps/bands/reserves, per-field
limits and certified device/OS or endpoint/account evidence.

The Provider profile is one exhaustive tagged union:

| Tag | Exact identity/accounting requirements |
|---|---|
| `LocalOperatingEnvelope` | model/material digest, local runtime/device cohort, deterministic tokenizer/processor or certified local opaque contract |
| `SystemOpaqueEnvelope` | historical AFM OS/SystemLanguageModel decode/recovery fixture only; the closed roster rejects it for new producer, registration, election, allocation or Attempt use |
| `SystemManagedRemoteOpaqueEnvelope` | PCC signed app-visible system-managed cohort, disclosure/quota/reasoning surface and conservative bound; hidden account/model fields forbidden |
| `RemoteOperatingEnvelope` | custom exact endpoint/account/region/model revision, tokenizer or conservative contract, input/output/tool/schema/modality/request caps, no redirect and terminal usage-observation semantics |

Unavailable presence matrices are tag-specific and typed; fields from another
tag, optimistic character division and silent redirect reject. Provider-owned
receipt exists only for `opaqueRuntimeExactCount`: pure L3 emits one
self-ID-free `BASContextAccountingRequest`, the owning Provider returns one
immutable `BASContextAccountingReceipt`, and L3 equality-reopens it before
emitting the final descriptor and `BASContextBudgetReceipt`. The deterministic
and conservative paths construct neither a `BASContextAccountingRequest` nor a
`BASContextAccountingReceipt`; L3 proves their respective evidence locally
and emits the same final budget-receipt family. Historical AFM bytes may decode
the bounded two-pass `AFMAccountingShape` only for migration/recovery negative
fixtures. No new producer, registration, election, allocation, materialization
or Attempt may select that tag; the current roster therefore never executes
its count-overload vector.

The accounting values have exactly one declaration each and follow the
existing package direction. Under existing owner `provider.package-boundary`,
`BehavioralAISubstrate/Sources/BASRuntimeCore/ProviderExecutionCore.swift`
declares the Provider-visible base protocol values:
`BASContextAccountingSection`, `BASContextCapacityTopology`,
`BASContextSafetyMarginProjection`,
`BASContextReasoningMode`, `BASContextAttachmentModality`,
`BASContextAttachmentGeometry`, `BASContextAttachmentAccountingInput`,
`BASContextHardLimitKind`,
`BASContextHardLimitUnit`, `BASContextHardLimitRelation`,
`BASContextCertifiedHardLimit`, `BASContextCertifiedLimitVector`,
`BASOpaqueContextAccountingShape`, `BASContextAccountingRequest`,
`BASContextAccountingFailureReason`,
`BASContextAccountingCountProjection`, `BASContextAccountingOutcome`, and
`BASContextAccountingReceipt`. Under existing owner `state.context-compiler`,
`BehavioralAISubstrate/Sources/BASOrchestration/ContextCompilerCore.swift`
declares the compiler-local proof/output values:

`BASContextRemainingCapacity`, and `BASContextBudgetReceipt`. RuntimeCore
never imports BASOrchestration; the compiler depends inward on these base

This is a controlled replacement of the still-unimplemented future sketch in
`2026-07-15-iphone-air-semantic-statelake-context.md`, not a coexisting second

validating initializer/factory and a custom decoder that rejects unknown,
missing, duplicate and wrong-tag fields; synthesized associated-value Codable
is forbidden. Every struct has exact `CodingKeys`, a throwing initializer and
a custom decoder. Their canonical stored-field sets are:

```text
BASOpaqueContextAccountingShape = providerWholeRequest(requestLayoutDigest) | afmFreshSession(countOverloadVectorDigest)
BASContextSafetyMarginProjection = sharedTotal(sharedCount) | splitInputOutput(inputCount,outputCount) | encoderOnly(encoderCount)
BASContextAccountingRequest = {schemaVersion,turnOperationRef,workspaceRef,workUnitRefArtifactID,attemptRefArtifactID,providerProfileArtifactID,providerCohortID,certifiedContextGeometryArtifactID,accountingContractDigest,opaqueAccountingShape,topology,safetyMargins,instructionBytes,transcriptBytes,promptBytes,toolContractBytes,schemaBytes,outputContractBytes,orderedAttachments,orderedSectionDigests,certifiedUpperBounds,certifiedUpperBoundsDigest,reasoningMode,visibleOutputReserve,privateReasoningReserve,protocolReserve,currentCapabilityEpoch}
BASContextAccountingCountProjection = sharedTotal(exactWholeRequestCount) | splitInputOutput(exactInputCount,requiredOutputReserveCount) | encoderOnly(exactEncoderCount)
BASContextAccountingOutcome = success(countProjection) | failure(reason)
BASContextAccountingReceipt = {schemaVersion,requestDigest,providerProfileArtifactID,providerCohortID,certifiedContextGeometryArtifactID,accountingContractDigest,topology,reasoningMode,currentCapabilityEpoch,outcome}
BASContextBudgetAccountingEvidence = deterministicTokenSpans(tokenizerArtifactID,tokenSpanProofDigest) | opaqueReceipt(accountingRequestArtifactID,accountingReceiptArtifactID) | certifiedConservativeUpperBound(certifiedBoundArtifactID,boundProofDigest)
BASContextCheckedLimitValue = exactObserved(value) | certifiedUpperBound(value,boundProofDigest)
BASContextBudgetReceipt = {schemaVersion,totalLimit,orderedAllocations,orderedCompressionArtifactIDs,contextCandidateDigest,providerProfileArtifactID,certifiedContextGeometryArtifactID,certifiedUpperBoundsDigest,topology,accountingEvidence,orderedByteSectionSpans,orderedSectionFingerprints,conservationProof,visibleOutputReserve,privateReasoningReserve,protocolReserve,hardPredicateVerdicts,omissionLedger,finalContextDescriptorDigest,remainingCapacity,currentCapabilityEpoch}
```

The seven accounting sections are canonical and appear exactly once, in enum
order, in the request digests, byte spans, fingerprints and section-count
hard-limit rows; spans are
non-overlapping, gap-free within their serialized section domain, checked for
`UInt64` overflow and bind the exact bytes used by the counter. The
`orderedHardLimits` vector is the sole authority for every certified cap: it
contains no parallel section-bound array or topology-cap scalar. Every digest
is lowercase 64-hex and every Artifact ID is reopened before use.
`BASContextRemainingCapacity` has an exact presence matrix:
`sharedTotal` permits only `sharedTotalCount`; `splitInputOutput` permits only
`inputCount + outputCount`; `encoderOnly` permits only `encoderCount`.
It is a checked, derived diagnostic projection and never a second cap or an
input to authorization. The equations are closed: shared remaining equals
`wholeRequestCapacity - (exactWholeRequestCount + visibleOutputReserve +
privateReasoningReserve + protocolReserve + sharedSafetyMargin)`; split input
remaining equals `inputCapacity - (exactInputCount + inputSafetyMargin)` and
split output remaining equals `outputCapacity -
requiredOutputReserveCount`; encoder remaining equals `encoderCapacity -
(exactEncoderCount + encoderSafetyMargin)`. Every addition and subtraction is
checked, every minuend is the unique matching `orderedHardLimits` capacity
row, and an underflow rejects. `exactWholeRequestCount`, `exactInputCount`, and
`exactEncoderCount` equal the corresponding accounting count in the
conservation proof; `requiredOutputReserveCount` equals the checked reserve
equation below. No receipt field may report or authorize Provider-claimed
"available" capacity.
`BASContextConservationProof` uses checked arithmetic and its equation digest
binds topology, observed/certified counts, all reserves, the topology-tagged
safety margins and the resulting capacity. Request safety-margin tag,
conservation-proof safety-margin tag, receipt topology and remaining-capacity
shape must all equal the selected topology. Hard-predicate verdicts are
canonical, unique by the
certified `limitID` and all must pass; an omission entry is canonical,
source-Artifact-bound and can never stand in for authorization or a counted
section. Every verdict is an exact bijection with one certified hard-limit
row and repeats its kind, optional Provider field ID, unit, relation and
certified value. Its unique matched row reopens the source-contract identity
before the verdict binds one tagged checked value. `exactObserved` is legal
only for a value directly measured or computed
from the canonical request bytes. `certifiedUpperBound` is legal only when the
selected signed profile/geometry carries that bound and the named proof digest
is reopened; it never claims that the upper bound was observed. Opaque exact
accounting uses its success projection for topology counts but uses certified
bounds for token/count dimensions the Provider does not expose. Conservative
accounting uses certified bounds; deterministic accounting may use exact token
spans. Request byte lengths, tool/schema/modality geometry, equality-required
reserves/margins and capability epoch remain exactly observed. The tag of the
checked value must agree with `accountingEvidence`; a caller cannot upgrade a bound
to exact evidence.
The common kinds separately require tool count, schema complexity, schema
bytes, modality count, every modality-geometry scalar, attachment bytes,
complete request bytes, each section/capacity/reserve and the capability
epoch. `providerSpecificField` is legal only when `providerFieldID` is
non-empty and equality-reopened from the selected profile's signed accounting
contract; it is never a caller-invented escape hatch. `orderedAttachments` is canonical by source Artifact ID and input
ordinal; each row binds exact bytes, content/preprocessing digests, one typed
modality-matching geometry and a certified input-count upper bound. Its
aggregate digest is the single `attachments` section digest. The certified
limit vector is profile/geometry-bound and contains a canonical,
unique-by-`limitID` hard-limit row for every applicable common and
Provider-specific field. Exactly one row maps to each of the seven sections:
`instructionCount`, `transcriptCount`, `promptCount`, `toolContractCount`,
`schemaCount`, `outputContractCount`, and `attachmentInputCount`. Its capacity
rows obey one closed presence matrix: `sharedTotal` has exactly one
`wholeRequestCapacity` row; `splitInputOutput` has exactly one
`inputCapacity` and one `outputCapacity` row; `encoderOnly` has exactly one
`encoderCapacity` row. All other capacity-kind rows are forbidden for that
topology. Thus section, topology, conservation and predicate checks reopen the
same row bytes rather than competing copies. No unused capacity in one
dimension compensates for another. Tool count and schema complexity/bytes,
modality count and each geometry scalar, attachment bytes, request bytes,
per-section and whole request are never collapsed into an aggregate pass.
The kind/relation matrix is closed. Section counts, tool/schema/modality/
geometry/attachment/request measurements and capacity rows use only
`lessThanOrEqual`. `visibleOutputReserve`, `privateReasoningReserve`,
`protocolReserve`, all four safety-margin kinds and `capabilityEpoch` use only
`equal`, so a required reserve cannot pass by shrinking to zero. For
`encoderOnly`, the three reserve rows are present as equality-to-zero rows,
`encoderSafetyMargin` alone is present, and shared/input/output safety rows are
forbidden. `sharedTotal` permits only `sharedSafetyMargin`; split permits
exactly `inputSafetyMargin` and `outputSafetyMargin`. A Provider-specific row
uses the relation frozen by its signed field contract; no other relation or
kind/relation pair decodes.

The retained legacy projection is diagnostic, never authorization.
`totalLimit` is derived only after the authoritative capacity rows pass: it is
the checked `Int(exactly wholeRequestCapacity)` for `sharedTotal`, checked
`Int(inputCapacity + outputCapacity)` for `splitInputOutput`, and checked
`Int(exactly encoderCapacity)` for `encoderOnly`. A missing/duplicate row,
`UInt64` addition overflow, or a value greater than `Int.max` rejects rather
than truncating. `orderedAllocations` is canonical, unique and sorted by
`BASContextBudgetClass.rawValue`; every integer is nonnegative, all classes
except `generationReserve` charge the input/shared/encoder dimension, and
`generationReserve` alone charges the output/shared dimension. Each row is an
exact projection of the compiler decision and cannot increase a certified
capacity. Compression Artifact IDs are canonical, unique and reopened.
`allocation(for:)` remains a pure read-only lookup and cannot authorize extra
capacity.
For `encoderOnly`, `visibleOutputReserve`, `privateReasoningReserve`, and
`protocolReserve` are all exactly zero, and the `generationReserve`
allocation's requested/admitted/truncated/compressed/reserved integers are all
zero. For `splitInputOutput`, `requiredOutputReserveCount` equals, with checked
arithmetic, visible output + private reasoning + protocol + the
`splitInputOutput.outputCount` safety margin; the independent input margin
charges only input. For `sharedTotal`, the single margin and all reserves
charge the one shared capacity. No margin or reserve can migrate between
dimensions.
Empty/duplicate/missing/out-of-order sections, modality/geometry mismatch,
overflow, a false or missing required predicate, a mismatched equation, or a topology-presence
violation rejects before allocation.

All values are self-ID-free and strict-Codable, with explicit `CodingKeys` and
schema-derived per-tag presence matrices. The request carries the canonical
complete candidate bytes, ordered digests, selected opaque shape and all
reserves, never a mutable session. `providerWholeRequest` requires its layout
digest and forbids an AFM overload vector. `afmFreshSession` requires the
certified count-overload-vector digest, and the AFM fresh-session shape
requires empty `transcriptBytes`; instructions, prompt, tools, schema and
reserves remain separately present so no role is double-counted.

Because the accounting request contains exact candidate/attachment bytes, its
Artifact is always encrypted and retention-classed `recovery72Hours` under the same
or narrower Workspace/App-Agent/purpose/erasure scope as its source content.
It is excluded from EventLog, analytics, learning, `auditProof` and
cross-Agent sharing, and is erased after materialization/reconciliation or its
finite purpose-specific maximum, never before its admitted minimum. The content-free receipt and digests may outlive the
request only as proof that counting occurred; they cannot reopen expired
plaintext or silently promote it to a longer retention class.

The Provider receipt has no accounting-proof union because its type is solely
the opaque-exact protocol. Success requires exactly the fields of its tagged
count projection; it carries no available/remaining-capacity scalar. It binds
the exact counts to the request/profile/cohort/geometry/
contract/topology/reasoning/capability epoch. Request topology, receipt
topology and success-projection tag must be equal, and the receipt reopens the
request's exact certified capacity-row set; any cross-tag substitution rejects
in both the validating initializer and decoder. `requiredOutputReserveCount`
is a pre-claim reservation, never actual generated-output usage. Terminal
output truth remains solely in the Provider usage-observation/reconciliation
receipt. A typed failure forbids every count; it makes that profile
pre-claim ineligible and produces neither a final descriptor nor a budget
receipt. The receipt carries no content, token IDs, invented spans or runtime
handle.

The only three-way proof union is `BASContextBudgetAccountingEvidence`, whose
tag is orthogonal to `sharedTotal`, `splitInputOutput`, and `encoderOnly`.
`deterministicTokenSpans` requires reproducible tokenizer and token-span proof,
forbids both accounting Artifact IDs and any conservative-bound proof;
`opaqueReceipt` requires both request and receipt Artifact IDs, equality-checks
the receipt's exact count projection, and forbids invented token spans;
`certifiedConservativeUpperBound` requires certified per-section and
topology-exact capacity rows, forbids both accounting Artifact IDs and any
exact-total claim.
All three success paths bind exact byte-section spans, fingerprints, topology
conservation, reserves, topology-tagged margins, hard predicates and omission ledger in the
final receipt without predicting its own Artifact ID or copying an editable
cap. Contract tests cover all three proof tags crossed with all three cap
topologies, wrong-tag field injection, missing/extra receipt identities,
opaque failure, PCC quota/reasoning-surface mismatch, incumbent AFM
compatibility-fixture empty-transcript/count-overload mismatch, and
materializer recheck before claim.

R5's `model` branch is further tagged `smallGroundingProposal` and requires a
proposal-only specialist profile with fixed reservoir, request/schema/source-
span roots and a bounded resource envelope. The Main Qwen, PCC, or future API
profile cannot substitute merely because it can generate text; it must be
separately certified for the same small-grounding role. Granite remains
dense-retrieval-only and KaLM remains rerank-only.
Deterministic, human/tool and `notRequired` branches remain valid and carry no
Provider receipt.

`classicML` binds an existing `BASCoreMLLayerHead` through a purpose-and-digest
allowlist plus exact input/output ABI. It is a bounded deterministic candidate
kind and cannot impersonate Qwen, PCC, MiniCPM, Granite, KaLM, a Provider
receipt or a portfolio role. No second Core ML registry is introduced.

W5 adapts the existing
`BehavioralAISubstrate/Sources/BASChatCompletionsAdapter/BASChatCompletionsOrganAdapter.swift`.
It may retain transport/codec mechanics only behind the governed tagged
profile, materialized request, nonsecret credential handle, authorized egress,
exact accounting/budget, terminal observation and same-operation query/reconcile
seams. Raw headers, caller token defaults, character estimates, unlimited caps
and ambiguous terminal status cannot cross the adapter membrane.

W4 adds the development-host hermetic conversion/certification slice using the
incumbent `BASCoreMLConversionContract`: stable download identity, offline
conversion, manifest/SBOM/license, exact tensor ABI, digest-before-load and
independent device certification for the exact local roster:
Granite-311M encoder → KaLM Nano reranker → MiniCPM5-1B text specialist →
Qwen3.5-4B Main. PCC and the retired incumbent AFM compatibility mechanism are
never converted, and MiniCPM-V/Granite-97M have no selectable production row.
The packaged
`BASContextClassifier.aimodel` is inventoried; a legacy 0.4.0 asset or an asset
whose tensors are selected via `.inputNames.first`/`.outputNames.first` is
rejected before load. A 0.4.1+ replacement must name every tensor and pass the
exact tensor ABI and current OS/runtime cohort before packaging.

Without a language model, deterministic persona formatting remains available
for structured deterministic/human/tool output:
neutral verified content → bounded L12 style/structure projection → L10
post-style invariant verification → ordinary release. Generative paraphrase
remains typed `externalProducerRequired`. Persona may never alter a fact,
number, uncertainty, warning, citation, permission or receipt.

#### E. Governed learning and data-flywheel closure

The SDK owns the complete governed learning protocol while every candidate
remains proposal-only. W1 freezes strict values under the existing
`state.snapshot-contracts`, `runtime.semantic-dag`, `runtime.certification` and
`production.cutover` owners: experience/exposure, `RewardEvidenceVector`,
credit/attribution, `DatasetManifest`, split/contamination evidence,
`TrainingJobManifest`, candidate identity, Policy-A, Evidence-B, OPE/shadow/
canary/rollback/reset/recovery and deletion/taint fanout. K3 owns only event
ordering, epochs, heads and CAS; Artifact Mesh stores immutable bodies.

Reward is a vector of independently evidenced task correctness, constraint and
safety compliance, calibrated uncertainty, user correction/approval, resource
cost and side effects; engagement, dependence, silence, dwell time and model
self-confidence are forbidden reward truth. Dataset manifests bind exact
source class/compartment, all seven cleaning gates, immutable train/eval/
holdout roots, ancestry/dedup/split-leakage/contamination proofs, purpose,
consent/deletion epochs and current eligibility.

`TrainingJobManifest` binds dataset/split/evidence roots, target base/profile,
objective family, verifier contracts, hyperparameter/resource envelope,
randomness/provenance, external trainer identity, output/candidate schema,
failure/restart semantics and admission prohibition. The evidence-shape matrix
is exact: SFT for independently eligible demonstrations; DPO/IPO/ORPO for
independently supported ordered pairs; KTO for calibrated binary desirability;
RLVR/GRPO only when an independent verifier's declared soundness domain covers
the rewarded subclaim; contextual bandit only for a logged finite action set
with propensities and support. Missing support yields no trainer substitution.
The external trainer computes gradients but cannot sign, admit, or cut over.

Policy-A is the currently installed policy/profile and pre-exposure decision.
Evidence-B is a separately committed post-exposure evidence root. Exploration
uses fixed-point bounded statistics, explicit propensities and finite support;
OPE, calibration, distribution-shift, side-effect, shadow and canary checks
consume both roots without rewriting them. Promotion is a separate certified
candidate followed by the incumbent cutover protocol. Rollback/reset and
deletion/taint fence all later consumers before asynchronous cleanup.

The incumbent disposition is decided now, not deferred to an implementer.
Each incumbent retains its existing code owner/path and can reach production
only through the listed incumbent authority seam:

The eight negative tests join `BASGovernedLearningContractTests.swift` and its
same-command non-empty W1 suite gate. No new learning queue, store or manager
may appear.

Learning is post-Attempt only. A verified outcome may become an immutable
candidate for a future snapshot only after eligibility, independent evidence,
credit, deletion/currentness, shadow/OPE and cutover gates. In particular,
same-operation feedback is forbidden: an operation cannot learn from, promote,
route with or
modify the evidence/candidate it is currently generating. The Möbius metaphor
means this delayed causal evidence flow through existing owners, not a fifth
ring or self-modifying loop.

#### G. Journal-first continuity, context, portfolio, and inquiry closure

This approved delta defines the **Journal-first Continuity Fabric** as a
composition of incumbent authorities, not another brain, persistence system,
or orchestration tier. Its recovery truth is exactly `K3/EventLog + encrypted
Artifact + owner receipts`. EventLog remains content-free, Artifact Mesh owns
immutable encrypted bodies, K3 owns current heads/CAS/fencing, and every
Provider, tool, effect, publication, deletion, cache, and Apple boundary keeps
its own typed receipt. The fabric creates no second Store, Manager, Router,
compiler, Agent bus, owner, wave, layer, ring, or plane.

The five recovery-quality labels `exactAppOwnedBytes`,
`deterministicReplay`, `semanticReconstruction`, `externalReconciliation`,
and `unavailable` are a derived, non-Codable UI projection over reopened
evidence. They never enter a reducer, grant authority, or upgrade uncertainty.
Qinao can reproduce app-owned committed bytes exactly; deterministically
replay pure work; reconstruct semantic intent from accepted state; reconcile
an external possible-start boundary through its owner; or honestly report
unavailable. It never claims to restore a Swift stack, dead process/PTY,
unsent hidden analysis, Provider-private KV, PCC hidden reasoning, OS-private
memory, secret, or ambient handle. This is the maximum honest approximation of
a virtual-machine snapshot without weakening iOS isolation.

**Plan before action and attention re-entry.** Every conversation has a
current immutable `Mission → Objective → WorkUnit → Attempt →
SolutionArtifact` graph, including a one-node micro-plan for a trivial reply.
Input normalization, requirement analysis, and read-only retrieval needed to
form the plan remain legal; before Provider, tool, state, effect, publication,
or release allocation, K3 must reopen the current mission-graph root, the
current predecessor receipts, and the exact Attempt fencing epoch. Recovery
keeps the stable WorkUnit identity, creates a fresh Attempt when required, and
never lets an old Attempt regain current authority.

Attention re-entry is derived from the existing `ContextContinuityManifest`,
nested `WorkUnitRecoveryCursor`, mission graph, K3 heads, and owner receipts.
Its bounded orientation projection answers exactly who, why, goal, completed,
evidence, pending, uncertain, next, and blocked. It is recomputed after
interruption, foreground return, rebase, user steering, or material snapshot
change; it is not a durable `AttentionManager`, second task graph, or hidden
chain-of-thought archive.

**Minimum-three-day recovery and durable conversation truth.** The retention
wire becomes exactly `neverPersist`, `ephemeral`, `recovery72Hours`,
`eligibleLearning72Hours`, `userDurable`, and `auditProof`.
`recovery72Hours` starts at the same trusted K3 commit as its retention
admission and computes `minimumRetainUntilMs = trustedStart + 259200000` with
a strictly later, finite, purpose-specific maximum. Terminal completion,
ordinary pruning, cache pressure, app backgrounding, archive, reboot, clock
rollback, or lack of memory may not shorten that minimum. It grants no
learning, sharing, cross-Agent, Provider-disclosure, memory, reward, or
training right. Explicit deletion, consent withdrawal, legal deletion, secret
detection, and privacy/security reclassification still fence reads and make
the body/key unreachable immediately while preserving only permitted
content-free proof. Process-local uncommitted scratch and unavailable hidden
runtime state remain `ephemeral`; plans and inquiry transcripts use
`userDurable` until explicit deletion.

`BASRetentionAdmissionReceipt` is the only min/max decision. A checkpoint,
continuity manifest, shell transcript, accepted model-output prefix, tool
invocation, or cache image references that receipt and cannot copy a second
expiry clock. Disk pressure evicts rebuildable indexes, embeddings, derived
projections, model/KV caches, and temporary downloads first. If the remaining
encrypted capacity cannot honor an admitted minimum, Qinao rejects new heavy
work with a typed capacity result rather than silently deleting committed
plans, messages, approvals, accepted output, or effect receipts.

**Independent adaptive context and turn maintenance.** The canonical context
identity is
`workspace × conversation × logicalAgent × role × workUnit × attempt ×
capsuleKind × capabilityProfile`. Each identity has an independent context
window, cancellation scope, history transform, cache identity, and exact
budget `min(advertised, empiricallyCertified) - reserves`; no window borrows
another window's private KV, quota, summary, budget, or mutable prompt state.
Every committed turn runs cheap deterministic maintenance: append canonical
facts and provenance, update mission/continuity heads, preserve hard
constraints and unresolved conflicts, and compact only derived projections.
Embedding, reranking, model-assisted extraction, and deeper ontology work may

## Task 0: Select and Pin the Only Convergence Predecessor

**Files:**

- Read: the current repository and all candidate worktree metadata.
- Create externally, never commit: `qinao-dual-space-source-selection-v1.json` with mode `0600`.
- Create after admission: one isolated `codex/` execution worktree.
- Do not modify production or controlled documents in this task.

**Interfaces:**

`QinaoDualSpaceSourceSelectionV1` must bind:

```text
schemaVersion
repositoryIdentity
selectedHEAD
selectedTree
approvedDesign = {path, commit, tree, blob, byteLength, sha256}
candidateComparisons[]
reviewerPrincipal
reviewerRole
issuedAt
expiresAt
nonce
signatureAlgorithm
signature
```

The frozen `approvedDesign` member remains the exact 2026-07-29 tuple. The
selected predecessor must already contain that byte-exact file; otherwise C0
rejects the predecessor rather than spending the single design-edge transition
on repairing an incomplete base. The approved 2026-08-02 supplemental tuple is
checked independently against Global Constraints and is the only file eligible
for the existing `QinaoDesignEdgeAdmissionReceiptV1` transition when absent.
The selected predecessor must already contain the exact 2026-07-23 governed-learning design blob
fixed in Global Constraints. C0 independently reopens and hashes it; absence,
wrong blob, wrong length, or wrong SHA-256 rejects the predecessor. There is no
third design edge and no extension of `QinaoDualSpaceSourceSelectionV1`.
This preserves the V1 selection schema and the nineteen-transition replay.

Canonical signed bytes are RFC 8785 JSON with the `signature` member omitted,
UTF-8 encoded, then SHA-256 digested and Ed25519-signed. The one external
admission trust root maps key fingerprints to disjoint
`source-selector`, `root-admission-signer`,
`design-edge-admission-signer`, `wave-bundle-reviewer`,
`wave-admission-signer`, `k4-evidence-signer`, and
`runtime-chain-signer` roles. A trust root contains public verification
material only and is never passed as a signing credential.

The independently reviewed external verifier checks repository identity,
approved-design tuple, reviewer role, signature, expiry, nonce uniqueness,
and selected commit/tree equality. It also, before requesting the root signature, stable-opens the governed-learning path from verifiedHEAD through the bound Git executable and requires blob `75a34022593ea2d85405021e75272d7c7f0c2af1`, byte length `185314`, and SHA-256 `e14375de67f7baf9bfe9c4e466b1182fbe906f849da0e260a37bd8bbd6554079`; absence or mismatch returns `rejected` and no signer call. It then asks only the protected
`root-admission-signer` provider to sign
`QinaoRootAdmissionReceiptV1`, which binds the selection blob, trust-root and
external-verifier executable digests, verified selector signer/role,
verified HEAD/tree, verification time, outcome, root signer/role, issue/expiry,
nonce, algorithm, and signature. This signed root receipt—not an unsigned
verification JSON—is the predecessor-chain root.

For this convergence replay, the record selects only comparison row 01's exact
committed predecessor. Rows 02-19 are unselected review-source snapshots and
cannot redefine `selectedHEAD/tree`. It may not select “latest,” a worktree
directory, an index tree, an uncommitted aggregate, or a mixed path set. If a
review-source delta must change, it becomes a newly committed/reviewed row
before selection is signed; no path-level mixing occurs during replay.

  ```bash
    --signing-provider-sha256 "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_ADMISSION_SIGNING_PROVIDER_SHA256" \
    --receipt "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_ADMISSION_RECEIPT"
  test "$("$QINAO_GIT_EXECUTABLE" write-tree)" = "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_TREE"
  "$QINAO_GIT_EXECUTABLE" diff --cached --check
  QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_INSTALLED_COMMIT=$(
    "$QINAO_BOOTSTRAP_CAS_BROKER" install-design-edge \
      --repository "$PWD" \
      --target-ref "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_TARGET_REF" \
      --base-commit "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_BASE_COMMIT" \
      --base-tree "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_BASE_TREE" \
      --candidate-tree "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_TREE" \
      --source-selection "$QINAO_SOURCE_SELECTION" \

      --commit-message "docs(qinao): admit biomimetic sovereign agent design"
  )
  "$QINAO_BOOTSTRAP_CAS_BROKER" verify-design-edge-install \
    --repository "$PWD" \
    --target-ref "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_TARGET_REF" \
    --base-commit "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_BASE_COMMIT" \
    --candidate-commit "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_INSTALLED_COMMIT" \
    --candidate-tree "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_TREE" \
    --receipt "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_ADMISSION_RECEIPT" \
    --trust-root "$QINAO_ADMISSION_TRUST_ROOT"
  test "$("$QINAO_GIT_EXECUTABLE" symbolic-ref -q HEAD)" = "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_TARGET_REF"
  test "$("$QINAO_GIT_EXECUTABLE" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_INSTALLED_COMMIT"
  test "$("$QINAO_GIT_EXECUTABLE" rev-parse HEAD^{tree})" = "$QINAO_DESIGN_EDGE_TREE"
  test -z "$("$QINAO_GIT_EXECUTABLE" status --porcelain)"
  ```

`draft-categories` is the sole repository-side producer of the four

worktree bytes. It excludes the four fixed category-evidence
import paths themselves from `reviewedRows` and `productionDiffRoot`, so none
of the four objects hashes itself or a sibling signature. It emits exactly
`create.json`, `extension.json`, `adapter.json`, and `fixture.json` as distinct
external regular non-symlink mode-`0600` files under an external mode-`0700`
directory that is create-only on first use and exact stable-reopen on retry.
The category status is derived from the complete diff:
nonempty matching rows require `status == "present"` with nonempty manifest
rows; an empty derived set requires signed `status == "notApplicable"`. No
new `manifest` enum literal is introduced. A caller cannot choose that status,
omit a category, or supply a destination repository path.

drafting. The runner recognizes that one exact closed path as a later evidence
output, excludes it from the category production diff alongside the four
category import paths, and rejects any other missing listed path. V2 has no
such exception because its bundle remains external. This rule cannot be
selected by a flag; it is derived only from the verified V1 lifecycle and the
exact `W0/w0.gates/1` row.
That V1 call requires `--base-commit` and `--base-tree` as equality witnesses;
all V2 calls prohibit both and derive the base solely from their verified
immediate predecessor terminal. The same conditional rule applies to draft,
review, and import.

Only the pinned external verifier exposes `review-wave-categories`. It
stable-opens all four static payloads, independently rederives the full
base/review-source-tree/path-list/design/category partition, and invokes only the
`wave-bundle-reviewer` role provider through four domain-separated durable
signing operations. For each category it create-only opens the signing claim,
generates and freezes issue/expiry/nonce plus the role/key/algorithm envelope,
forms the one true canonical signing preimage, and only then contacts the
provider. Its `stableSemanticInputRoot` binds category, repository identity,
fixed repository import path, immediate predecessor, base commit/tree,
approved-design blob, path-list root, production-diff root, reviewed-row root,
and tool identities; it excludes candidate commit/tree/refs, time, nonce,
external output paths, process identity, and retry count. It writes exactly
the four same-named signed files into a different external mode-`0700`
directory that is create-only on first use and exact stable-reopen on retry;
partial completion is
recoverable one category at a time, but import remains all-or-nothing. Each
operation has one fixed external output path and obeys the common signing
transaction contract. No signer output path is inside the repository.

```text

```

`import-reviewed-categories` stable-opens and verifies all four complete
signed objects before publishing any candidate byte, rederives their fixed
candidate paths from the closed slice registry, and delegates the four held
descriptors and raw bytes to the path-scoped evidence-import broker. The
broker create-only freezes them in its immutable content-addressed namespace
and returns exactly one opaque line
`qinao-category-import-v1:<lowercase-64-hex-root>`. Standard error alone may
carry diagnostics; missing, extra, multiline, noncanonical, or changed output
fails. Exact retry returns the same handle. The token grants no authority and
is useful only because the broker reopens the corresponding immutable bytes,
transaction journal, fixed paths, signing-claim identities, and complete
four-object root. A caller cannot construct a working handle from raw paths or
digests alone.

`materialize-review-row` accepts only
`--verified-category-import-handle OPAQUE_HANDLE`; it never accepts a signed
category directory or four raw category paths. It asks the broker to stable-
open the held descriptors/bytes and revalidates the transition, predecessor,
path-list, category roots, signing claims, and import-journal root immediately
before writing its private index. Thus replacement of the reviewed directory
after verification is irrelevant. The broker creates or stable-reopens
byte-identical inert copies only in that isolated transition materialization
namespace; it never scans or overwrites the ambient worktree. “All-or-nothing” is
a staging-eligibility barrier, not a fictitious four-file atomic rename:
partial exact imports may exist after a crash, but no candidate is stageable
until all four final bytes match the one reviewed set. Import copies held raw
bytes without JSON re-encoding. It cannot accept a
destination argument, overwrite a mismatch, follow a symlink, import a
partial set, sign, directly stage, directly write a Git object, or mutate a
ref. Its four-file
transaction journal is external and content-addressed; recovery either
finishes the exact four-copy set or removes only never-published temporary
files. Once any final candidate path exists, every existing final must match
the same reviewed set or the operation quarantines. The checker later proves
that the staged tree contains exactly those bytes and that all four evidence
roots match the derived candidate diff. Neither V1 nor V2 category evidence
binds its containing candidate commit/tree/ref; bundle/receipt layers bind
those identities after import, preventing a category-to-candidate self-hash
cycle.
