```bash
"$QINAO_ADMITTED_PROTECTED_PYTHON" \
  scripts/run_qinao_wave_admission.py draft-categories \
  --root "$PWD" \
  --candidate-path-list docs/superpowers/evidence/qinao-dual-space-w0-gates-paths.txt \
  --source-selection "$QINAO_SOURCE_SELECTION" \
  --trust-root "$QINAO_ADMISSION_TRUST_ROOT" \
  --previous-receipt "$QINAO_PREVIOUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT" \
  --wave W0 --wave-slice-id w0.gates --sequence-ordinal 1 \
  --base-commit "$QINAO_W0_BASE_COMMIT" \
  --base-tree "$QINAO_W0_BASE_TREE" \
  --unsigned-category-directory "$QINAO_UNSIGNED_CATEGORY_DIRECTORY"
"$QINAO_EXTERNAL_ADMISSION_VERIFIER" review-wave-categories \
  --unsigned-category-directory "$QINAO_UNSIGNED_CATEGORY_DIRECTORY" \
  --signed-category-directory "$QINAO_SIGNED_CATEGORY_DIRECTORY" \
  --path-list docs/superpowers/evidence/qinao-dual-space-w0-gates-paths.txt \
  --source-selection "$QINAO_SOURCE_SELECTION" \
  --previous-receipt "$QINAO_PREVIOUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT" \
  --repository "$PWD" --trust-root "$QINAO_ADMISSION_TRUST_ROOT" \
  --wave W0 --wave-slice-id w0.gates --sequence-ordinal 1 \
  --base-commit "$QINAO_W0_BASE_COMMIT" \
  --base-tree "$QINAO_W0_BASE_TREE" \
  --signing-provider "$QINAO_WAVE_BUNDLE_REVIEW_SIGNING_PROVIDER" \
  --signing-provider-sha256 "$QINAO_WAVE_BUNDLE_REVIEW_SIGNING_PROVIDER_SHA256"
QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_HANDLE=$(
"$QINAO_ADMITTED_PROTECTED_PYTHON" \
  scripts/run_qinao_wave_admission.py import-reviewed-categories \
  --root "$PWD" \
  --candidate-path-list docs/superpowers/evidence/qinao-dual-space-w0-gates-paths.txt \
  --source-selection "$QINAO_SOURCE_SELECTION" \
  --trust-root "$QINAO_ADMISSION_TRUST_ROOT" \
  --previous-receipt "$QINAO_PREVIOUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT" \
  --wave W0 --wave-slice-id w0.gates --sequence-ordinal 1 \
  --base-commit "$QINAO_W0_BASE_COMMIT" \
  --base-tree "$QINAO_W0_BASE_TREE" \
  --signed-category-directory "$QINAO_SIGNED_CATEGORY_DIRECTORY"
)
QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_ROOT=${QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_HANDLE#qinao-category-import-v1:}
test "$QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_ROOT" != "$QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_HANDLE"
test "${#QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_ROOT}" = 64
case "$QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_ROOT" in
  ''|*[!0-9a-f]*) exit 1 ;;
  *) ;;
esac
"$QINAO_GIT_PREPARATION_BROKER" materialize-review-row \
  --transition-id 03 \
  --source-selection "$QINAO_SOURCE_SELECTION" \
  --verified-category-import-handle "$QINAO_W0_CATEGORY_IMPORT_HANDLE" \
  --omit-until-reviewed \
    docs/superpowers/evidence/qinao-dual-space-w0-gates-wave-bundle.json
```

For each V2 Wave registry row it expands the same three category modes plus
`materialize-review-row`, with the row-derived path list/wave/slice/ordinal,
no base arguments, its exact four fixed V2 import paths, and no omitted path.
The meta-test expands all fourteen rows and requires exactly fourteen V2 plus
one W0 sequences, each `draft -> review -> import -> materialize` before its
first candidate-tree write. Transition 04 (Ledger migration) is explicitly
absent from this expansion and uses its non-Wave candidate verifier.
That verifier has one exceptional W0 prerequisite: it independently reopens
the migration-materialized `QinaoK4IOS27PlatformSpikeV1` and requires
`status == supportedExactProfile`, the approved supplemental design blob,
the signed physical-device profile digest, current expiry, and the exact
verified evidence-import handle. A typed-disabled result remains valid
diagnostic evidence but cannot produce the migration terminal, close W0, or
be substituted by an in-process profile. This stronger policy is activated
atomically by Task 2; historical V1/W0 gate tooling before that edge remains
verifiable but cannot be claimed as final W0 closure.

`draft-bundle` is the sole non-authoritative producer of canonical unsigned
Wave bundle bytes. Schema dispatch comes only from the verified predecessor
and Ledger lifecycle, never a schema flag. Historical Task-1/W0 V1 requires
the exact base commit/tree plus four manifest/disposition arguments, prohibits
all four V2 candidate/ref arguments, and permits only its fixed reviewed-
bundle repository import path to be the one not-yet-created path-list member. Its
wave/slice/ordinal arguments are required equality witnesses for the derived
`W0`/`w0.gates`/`1` literals, not selectors. Every post-migration V2 call
requires the four candidate/ref arguments, prohibits base arguments and the
four caller-supplied
category arguments, and discovers exactly one Create/Extension/Adapter/
Fixture manifest-or-disposition from the candidate-tree Ledger admission refs
for the closed slice/ordinal. Missing, duplicate, cross-slice, or unreferenced
category evidence fails. V2 draft bytes contain only the static requirement
above; no challenge/run/Result/retention/finalization field is accepted.

The unsigned output obeys the external mode-`0600`, stable-open,
exclusive-create contract. A resumed call may return success only after
rederiving byte-identical canonical content at the same path; it never
overwrites. The mode cannot sign, issue a challenge, create a controller
claim, run protected validation, move a ref, or write a report/receipt.

The non-authoritative candidate-preparation utility has exactly this CLI:

```text
prepare_qinao_v2_wave_candidate.py
  --git-executable ABSOLUTE_CANONICAL_GIT_EXECUTABLE
  --root PATH
  --source-selection PATH
  --trust-root PATH
  --previous-receipt PATH
  --candidate-tree GIT_TREE
  --candidate-path-list PATH
  --wave W1_TO_W6
  --wave-slice-id CLOSED_SLICE_ID
  --sequence-ordinal POSITIVE_INTEGER
  --commit-message EXACT_MESSAGE
```

It accepts V2-to-V2 slices only. The trusted source selection supplies the
repository identity. Immediate-predecessor handling is phase-dispatched:

- For W1, the utility treats `QinaoLedgerV2MigrationTerminalReceiptV1` only as
  a protected-structural predecessor witness. That closed wire has no signer
  or signature fields. The utility reopens and exact-validates its schema and
  domain root, repository identity, fixed live `targetRefName`,
  `candidateCommit`/`candidateTree`, installed Owner-Ledger blob, and
  authorization-root structure. It does not claim or synthesize a signer or
  signature, and the witness plus prepared ref grants no admission. The
  external `wave-admission-controller` independently verifies the protected
  claim and evidence-store authorization during `admit-wave`.
- For W2–W6, the utility Ed25519-verifies the immediate
  `QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV2` under the trusted `wave-admission-signer`
  role/schema and derives target/base solely from `targetRefInstallation`:
  `targetRefName`, `installedCommit`, and `installedTree`.

The utility reopens the source selection, trust root, and phase-appropriate
predecessor receipt, then requires the derived target ref to equal the fixed
`refs/heads/codex/qinao-admitted-controlled-convergence` literal. It
rejects a caller-chosen branch, detached HEAD, abbreviated ref, tag,
remote-tracking ref, symbolic-ref chain, pseudoref, unverified predecessor,
or predecessor/schema mismatch. The prepared ref must equal
`refs/qinao/prepared/wave-v2/` followed by
`lowerHex(SHA256(RFC8785([repositoryIdentity,targetRefName,waveSliceID,
sequenceOrdinal,baseCommit,candidateTree])))`.
That ref is explicitly non-authoritative: it only keeps the candidate Git
object reachable until the existing external `wave-admission-controller`
finishes or reconciles the transaction.

The utility requires `targetRef == HEAD`, target-ref OID/base commit, base
tree, index tree/candidate tree, candidate path-list, and staged-path set to
agree before it writes an object. It rejects shallow history, replace refs,
grafts, missing or unreadable parent/tree/blob objects, unsafe Git environment
overrides, signing hooks/config, and a non-clean unstaged path from the closed
candidate set. It creates a one-parent commit over the
already written candidate tree with the exact supplied message, fixed identity
`Qinao Wave Candidate <qinao-wave-candidate@invalid>`, no optional headers,
and author/committer timestamp equal to the base commit's committer Unix second
plus one in `+0000`. The canonical commit bytes are therefore deterministic.
It then create-only installs the exact prepared ref. If interrupted after
object write but before ref creation, rerunning produces the same OID. If the
prepared ref already exists, it writes nothing and reopens its commit, parent,
tree, message, identity, and timestamp, then independently recomputes the ref
name from the reopened repository identity, inherited predecessor, and
supplied closed slice/ordinal; any mismatch fails. The caller never supplies a
target ref, base identity, or prepared ref. On success stdout is exactly one
ASCII line
`FULL_TARGET_REF<TAB>FULL_BASE_COMMIT<TAB>FULL_BASE_TREE<TAB>`
`FULL_CANDIDATE_COMMIT<TAB>FULL_PREPARED_REF<LF>` and stderr carries
diagnostics only. No abbreviated OID, whitespace inside any token, second
line, or additional stdout byte is legal. The utility never moves the target
ref, edits the index/worktree, signs, admits, writes a receipt, or deletes a
ref.

`--git-executable` is mandatory exactly once. The utility validates it as the
absolute canonical regular non-symlink executable bound by
`QINAO_GIT_EXECUTABLE`, uses only those bytes for every Git subprocess, and
requires the executable and every parent directory to be root-owned and
non-writable by the executing security subject. It rechecks path and
stable-opened descriptor identity around every invocation and constructs an
explicit Git environment with `PATH` absent. Missing, duplicate,
relative, symlinked, non-executable, noncanonical or PATH-selected Git fails
before any object/ref read or write.

For `report`, `verify-receipt`, `review-wave-bundle`, and `admit-wave`, V2's
four-element identity set is `candidate-tree` plus the three bracketed
candidate/ref arguments. Task 1's V1 W0 invocation keeps its historical
candidate-tree argument, must omit the other three, and rejects any one of
them; every post-migration V2 invocation requires all four. V2 independently
reopens the immediate predecessor and requires the candidate/ref arguments'
target ref and base commit/tree to equal that predecessor's installed values;
those arguments cannot select a different chain. It then
requires `candidateCommit^{tree} == candidateTree`, exactly one parent equal
to bundle `baseCommit`, and the deterministic commit metadata above. Fresh
bundle review and Report require prepared-ref OID equal to candidate commit
and target-ref OID equal to base commit. Fresh `admit-wave` starts from that
state; a resumed call accepts only the exact claim/ref states in the closed
recovery matrix below. `verify-receipt` instead requires target-ref OID equal
to candidate commit and the prepared ref absent, exactly as the signed
installation terminal states. Missing, partial, same-tree/different-commit,
or substituted ref input fails.

The trusted base/candidate Ledger lifecycle, not a caller flag, selects the
Wave schema. Task 1's last V1-to-V1 W0 gate may emit a canonical unsigned
`QinaoWaveCandidateReportV1` and matching
`QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV1`. The Task-2 V1-to-V2 transition emits no Wave
report or Wave receipt; it emits only the separately governed migration
terminal receipt described below. Every V2-to-V2 Wave after that transition
must emit `QinaoWaveCandidateReportV2` and
`QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV2`, and no new Wave V1 object is legal. The
repository runner writes its unsigned report outside the repository. The
independently pinned external verifier's `admit-wave` command must
independently rederive the base/index/candidate tree, both tree-opened
Ledgers, bundle and tool blobs, exact path-list/diff, categories,
prerequisites, schema version, and predecessor; it does not trust the
candidate report as authority. For historical V1 W0 only, that verification
may directly precede the protected `wave-admission-signer` operation. For V2,
`admit-wave` is the pinned front end to the already owned external
`wave-admission-controller`: after protected validation it resumes the one
durable operation claim, performs the sole target-ref CAS, reopens the
installed commit/tree/Ledger, retires the prepared ref, and only then asks the
same role-scoped signer for the terminal receipt signature. It assembles and
durably writes the external mode-`0600` receipt bytes before returning. The
repository runner's `verify-receipt` mode then verifies the final bytes,
schema lifecycle, live installed target ref, and exact commit/tree bindings.
A trust root never signs, and neither repository code nor ordinary PR CI
receives signing credentials.

`ordinary-report` is the fixed test-trust, V2, unsigned/unadmitted exception
described in Steps 1G/1J; it cannot consume or emit production authority and
cannot be used as a schema bridge.
`verify-ledger-migration` only verifies the incumbent external controller's
V1-to-V2 terminal receipt, immediate complete V1 predecessor chain, target
ref CAS, and exact candidate commit/tree; it cannot create a commit, run the
migration, install a Ledger, or move a ref.
`verify-ledger-migration-candidate` is the distinct non-Wave pre-controller
eligibility route. It derives the complete base-to-candidate path/mode/blob
diff, requires exactly the Task-2 controlled-document/Ledger/generated-mirror/
K4-evidence closure, independently proves zero production Swift/SQL/Rust/C/C++
delta, verifies the V1-to-V2 Ledger projection and protected bootstrap policy,
and rejects every extra or missing path. It consumes no Task-1 W0 category
evidence and emits no replacement category object, bundle, report, receipt,
signature, Git object, or ref effect. The migration requirement and terminal
receipt bind its roots; Wave category evidence remains exclusive to the
historical W0 Wave and fourteen post-migration V2 Waves.
`verify-protected-review` fixes
the operation to `bootstrap.amendment3-protected-review`, derives the managed
route internally, and verifies two surface challenges, terminal/retention
receipts, and their aggregate pair receipt. It cannot accept a caller-selected
tier/operation, issue any artifact, or mutate state. None of these modes
widens the Wave report/receipt schemas.

Every signing provider exposes only its fixed schema/role operation, accepts
requests only through the pinned external verifier identity, and independently
checks the request digest/role envelope before using its protected key. It is
not a general `sign(bytes)` executable and cannot be called directly by a
candidate workflow or repository script.

Every external role-scoped signature in this plan uses one common durable
signing-transaction contract. It covers root admission, design-edge review,
historical V1 and V2 category-evidence review, historical V1 and V2 bundle
review, historical V1 admission, K4 evidence, and the W6 runtime chain. V2
admission-receipt signing remains nested inside its stronger controller
operation claim but obeys the same publish/recovery rules. The
domain-separated request key is:

```text
signingOperationKey = lowerHex(SHA256(
  ASCII("QINAO-EXTERNAL-SIGNING-OPERATION-V1") || 0x00 ||
  RFC8785([
    role, schema, repositoryIdentity, stableSemanticInputRoot,
    renewalGeneration,
    trustRootDigest, externalVerifierDigest, signingProviderDigest
  ])
))

signingRequestKey =
lowerHex(SHA256(
  ASCII("QINAO-EXTERNAL-SIGNING-REQUEST-V1") || 0x00 ||
  RFC8785([
    role, schema, canonicalUnsignedPreimageStoredSHA256,
    renewalGeneration,
    repositoryIdentity, trustRootDigest,
    externalVerifierDigest, signingProviderDigest
  ])
))
```

`stableSemanticInputRoot` is the operation-specific closed root of all stable
selection/commit/tree/receipt/design/path/category/tool/evidence inputs; each
role schema defines it and the verifier independently derives it. It excludes
envelope issue/expiry time, nonce, unsigned/signed output paths and bytes,
process/task identity, and retry count. `renewalGeneration` is a separate
nonnegative integer: zero for the first signing operation and otherwise legal
only under the renewal protocol below. For every provider-produced envelope,
the signed existing `nonce` string has the closed form
`qinao-r<renewalGeneration>.<base64url-96-bit-random>`; this binds the
generation without adding a field to any frozen V1 or V2 wire. The verifier
first derives
`signingOperationKey`, create-only opens that claim, and atomically freezes the
canonical unsigned preimage, its generated issue/expiry/nonce, the derived
`signingRequestKey`, `authorizationEffectiveAt`, and the one fixed output path
before contacting the provider. `authorizationEffectiveAt` comes from the
incumbent verifier/controller trusted clock and must satisfy every relevant
input's `issuedAt <= authorizationEffectiveAt < expiresAt` plus trust-role,
policy-epoch, revocation, and currentness checks. Thus restart can locate the
claim from stable inputs even when both the local preimage and output file are
missing.

Every unsigned/signed output path is generation-qualified and coordinator-
derived, never caller-selected. Beneath the pinned artifact root the exact
layout is:

```text
<artifactRoot>/<sourceSelectionSHA256>/t<zero-padded-transitionID>/signing/
  <closedFamilySlug>/<stableSemanticInputRoot>/r<20-digit-generation>/
    unsigned.json
    signed.json
```

The four category operations use one closed set layout so the existing
directory interface remains exact:

```text
.../signing/category-set/<categorySetSemanticRoot>/r<20-digit-generation>/
  unsigned/{create.json,extension.json,adapter.json,fixture.json}
  signed/{create.json,extension.json,adapter.json,fixture.json}
```

All four category claims share the derived set generation, retain their
domain-separated category operation/request keys, and become import-eligible
only as one complete set; partial provider recovery stays per category. A
category-set renewal advances all four together and leaves the prior set
immutable. No
free-form name becomes a path component. The coordinator derives these paths
from verified registry/claim data, proves every ancestor is the expected
mode-`0700` non-symlink directory on the pinned artifact-root identity, and
opens each mode-`0600` leaf create-only. The common signing claim freezes that
one generation's exact two paths. Old generation directories and bytes remain
immutable; renewal uses only the uniquely derived next directory, never
overwrites or reuses an old `$QINAO_*_OUTPUT`. All output variables in lower
conformance oracles are aliases resolved by this derivation, not environment
choices. Concurrent sessions derive the same next path and join the same
claim; a supplied path, alternate zero-padding, symlink, second live head, or
path/claim mismatch quarantines.

The durable claim advances `prepared -> providerRequested -> signed ->
published`. The provider may process a request key at most once. On an unknown
provider or publish outcome, the verifier queries that exact operation claim
and provider request and recovers the byte-identical signed bytes; it never
changes nonce/path, creates another key, or asks for a second signature.
Existing exact output is stable-opened and reused; missing output after
`signed` is republished from the claim;
partial, symlinked, wrong-mode, different-byte, different-path, or different-
claim output is quarantined. Consequently no executable ceremony may use
`test ! -e OUTPUT` as a restart blocker or overwrite an existing output.

**Expiry, recovery, and renewal are closed.** Expiry gates creation of the
claim that authorizes an operation, not safe completion of that already
claimed byte-exact operation. If the exact signing or controller claim was
durably opened while all of its inputs were unexpired, recovery may cross wall
expiry only to finish that same frozen request, publish or reopen the same
bytes, complete the already authorized target-ref CAS, retire its prepared
ref, and persist its one terminal. It may not change an input, open another
claim, reissue a challenge, repeat an external effect, select a new candidate,
or use the expired artifact to begin a downstream operation. If the required
signing or controller claim did not exist before expiry, the operation is
ineligible; intended future work and a local draft/import/prepared ref are not
claims.

A terminal admission, migration, root, or design receipt whose installation
and initial verification completed under such a timely claim remains
immutable historical chain evidence after its envelope expires. Later
transitions reverify its signature, installed commit/tree/ref, predecessor
continuity, trust/revocation/policy epochs, and current live requirements;
they do not renew or reinterpret that terminal receipt. This historical rule
never lets a stale/unrooted signed selection, unconsumed category, bundle,
runtime chain, or other prerequisite start a new effect. After a timely root-
admission terminal, every later command's required `--source-selection`
argument must be byte-identical to the selection digest bound by that root
receipt. Its temporal eligibility is rechecked at the root claim's frozen
`authorizationEffectiveAt`, not against the later transition's wall clock;
the later claim still rechecks current trust, revocation, policy, receipt-chain,
and live-operation requirements. A different selection or a selection never
accepted by a timely root claim remains ineligible.

Renewal is available only for a signed prerequisite that expired before any
downstream signing, controller, or effect claim consumed it. The incumbent
signing service must atomically prove the prior generation is
`terminalExpiredUnconsumed`, prove no downstream claim or ref effect exists,
and open exactly `renewalGeneration = prior + 1`. Stable semantic payload
bytes remain identical; only the existing issue/expiry/nonce/signature
envelope and the generation-bound operation/request keys change.
Skipping/reusing a generation, renewing while a downstream claim exists, or
presenting two live generations is corruption. Category-set or historical-W0
in-tree bundle renewal retires only the old non-authoritative prepared ref,
rematerializes from the same immutable review-source row with the renewed
broker handle, and therefore derives a new tree/commit before any controller
claim. External V2 bundle renewal keeps the candidate commit/tree fixed but
regenerates its static report. Runtime-chain renewal is legal only before the
Apple bundle-review claim opens and keeps the exact six terminal receipts
fixed. Once the corresponding bundle-review or controller claim exists, all
three recover its frozen generation instead of renewing.

Category and external-prerequisite temporal eligibility is deliberately
one-way. The first bundle-review claim may open only while every category and
fresh prerequisite is unexpired; it freezes their exact bytes/digests,
generation/claim identities, and validity result in a
`bundleInputEligibilityRoot` at that claim's
`authorizationEffectiveAt`. From then on, those inputs are immutable static
review evidence for that exact bundle semantic root, not independently
renewable leases. A later controller claim verifies an unexpired bundle
generation and the frozen eligibility root at the original bundle-review
time, while independently rechecking current trust, policy, revocation,
candidate, ref, and live-operation requirements. It does not re-evaluate a
category's wall-clock expiry. If the bundle itself expires unconsumed, bundle
renewal may reuse the same eligibility root even though a subordinate
category/prerequisite has since expired; it cannot change any subordinate
byte. If a category expires before the first bundle-review claim, the category
must renew and any in-tree candidate must be rebuilt before that claim. This
closes both category -> bundle -> controller and runtime-chain -> Apple-bundle
-> Apple-controller pause boundaries without allowing a stale leaf to start a
new semantic review.

The externally authored source selection is not automatically renewable. If
it expires before the root signing claim opens, the source selector must issue
a new signed V1 selection over the exact same closed comparison rows; the
coordinator derives a new selection-digest namespace and restarts at
transition 01 without reusing an old claim. If the root claim opened in time,
it may finish exactly as above. No app, model, coordinator, or signing provider
extends an expiry or signs for the selector.

K4 uses the same rule until migration admission. If its evidence expires
before the migration controller claim, envelope renewal is legal only when a
fresh live-equality probe proves the held unsigned observation bytes,
supported-profile/design identities, and every result-bundle digest remain
byte-identical; it then renews only the envelope and rematerializes transition
04. If a fresh probe changes any semantic observation byte, it is not renewal:
after proving the old operation is `terminalExpiredUnconsumed` with no
downstream claim/effect, the incumbent service marks it
`terminalSupersededUnconsumed`, opens a new K4 semantic operation/root at
generation zero, retires the old non-authoritative prepared candidate, and
materializes only the newly reviewed handle. The external claim metadata
binds the old/new semantic roots as a supersession edge without adding a K4
wire field or authority family. Unknown old outcomes must reconcile before
either path. If the migration claim opened in time, only that exact generation
may finish. After the migration
terminal admits the exact K4 evidence blob, that blob is historical platform-
design evidence rather than a standing authorization lease. W5 may reference
it after envelope expiry only by proving the migration terminal binds the
identical blob/profile/design and by having the incumbent W5 controller
freshly revalidate the live device, SDK, entitlement, process, transport,
policy, and revocation profile before opening its own claim. A live profile
mismatch yields the typed disabled outcome; it cannot silently renew,
substitute, or downgrade K4.

The runtime chain has two ordered consumers without a renewal dead end.
Transition 18 must open its Apple bundle-review claim while one runtime-chain
generation is unexpired, or recover that exact claim, and its bundle claim and
terminal receipt bind that exact generation, chain digest,
`bundleInputEligibilityRoot`, and original `authorizationEffectiveAt`.
Transition 19 then treats that Apple-bound chain
as historical predecessor evidence: all five consumers independently reopen
and cryptographically verify the same chain and Apple binding, but do not
require the chain envelope to remain unexpired a second time. They still
require the Apple receipt, policy/trust/revocation epochs, and all live
certification requirements to be current. Therefore a pause after Apple and
before certification neither renews a consumed generation nor deadlocks; a
different chain or an Apple receipt without the timely binding fails.

No signer or reviewer publishes directly into a repository path. Historical
W0/V1 reviewed-bundle bytes, signed category evidence, and minimized K4
evidence all first land at fixed external mode-`0600` claim output paths and
are then stable-opened once by the evidence-import broker. That broker returns
the schema-specific opaque handle
`qinao-w0-bundle-import-v1:<64hex>`,
`qinao-category-import-v1:<64hex>`, or
`qinao-k4-import-v1:<64hex>` over its immutable held descriptors, exact raw
bytes, claim identities, fixed repository destinations, and transaction root.
Candidate materialization accepts only those handles and reopens the held
bytes through the broker immediately before its private-index write; it never
retrusts a signer-output path. The handles are content locators, not
capabilities, signatures, or admission authority. Those Git blobs are never
signer output paths, cannot cause signing, and must equal the broker-held
external signed bytes exactly.
This signing transaction is an
idempotency/recovery mechanism for incumbent roles, not a signer, state
authority, receipt family, SDK component, or license for repository code to
publish signatures.

```text
qinao-external-admission-verifier admit-wave
  --report PATH
  --bundle PATH
  --source-selection PATH
  --previous-receipt PATH
  --repository PATH
  --candidate-tree GIT_TREE
  [--candidate-commit GIT_COMMIT]
  [--target-ref-name GIT_REF]
  [--prepared-ref-name GIT_REF]
  --trust-root PATH
  [--external-prerequisite NAME=PATH]...
  --signing-provider PATH
  --signing-provider-sha256 HEX
  --receipt PATH
```

The bundle binds the previous receipt, base commit/tree, reviewed path-list
blob, four current category blobs, approved design blob, exact wave, and tool
blob identities. In V1 and for every non-K4 V2 prerequisite, its frozen
`externalPrerequisites[]` member is a lexicographically name-sorted array of
`{name, schema, blobDigest, requiredOutcome}`. The scheduled K4 V2 slice uses
only the exact specialized requirement/verified union defined below; it may
not be truncated to that four-field generic row. An empty array is explicit.
Every non-empty entry is supplied as one repeatable
`--external-prerequisite NAME=PATH` argument to `draft-bundle`, bundle review,
`report`, external `admit-wave`, and `verify-receipt`; duplicate names,
missing or additional arguments, any byte difference across those five
consumers, and order-normalization ambiguity fail.

Task 1's final historical V1 W0 bundle may enter its own candidate path list:
V1 does not bind the candidate commit/tree, and its production-diff root
excludes evidence bytes, so that one frozen path has no self-hash edge. Every
V2 Wave bundle is different: before report generation, an independent
reviewer approves its external mode-`0600` unsigned bytes and the external
verifier obtains only a `wave-bundle-reviewer` signature. The complete signed
V2 bundle remains external, never enters a candidate path list or Git tree,
and binds the already prepared candidate commit/tree plus protected target
and prepared refs. Its exact interface also accepts the same repeatable
optional prerequisite:

```text
qinao-external-admission-verifier review-wave-bundle
  --unsigned-bundle PATH
  --path-list PATH
  --source-selection PATH
  --previous-receipt PATH
  --repository PATH
  --trust-root PATH
  [--candidate-commit GIT_COMMIT]
  [--candidate-tree GIT_TREE]
  [--target-ref-name GIT_REF]
  [--prepared-ref-name GIT_REF]
  [--external-prerequisite NAME=PATH]...
  --signing-provider PATH
  --signing-provider-sha256 HEX
  --output PATH
```

The following is the executable post-migration V2 empty-prerequisite case;
Task 1/W0 uses the historical V1 form without the commit/ref arguments:

```bash
"$QINAO_EXTERNAL_ADMISSION_VERIFIER" review-wave-bundle \
  --unsigned-bundle "$QINAO_UNSIGNED_WAVE_BUNDLE" \
  --path-list "$QINAO_CURRENT_WAVE_PATH_LIST" \
  --source-selection "$QINAO_SOURCE_SELECTION" \
  --previous-receipt "$QINAO_PREVIOUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT" \
  --repository "$PWD" \
  --trust-root "$QINAO_ADMISSION_TRUST_ROOT" \
  --candidate-commit "$QINAO_CURRENT_CANDIDATE_COMMIT" \
  --candidate-tree "$QINAO_CURRENT_CANDIDATE_TREE" \
  --target-ref-name "$QINAO_CURRENT_TARGET_REF" \
  --prepared-ref-name "$QINAO_CURRENT_PREPARED_REF" \
  --signing-provider "$QINAO_WAVE_BUNDLE_REVIEW_SIGNING_PROVIDER" \
  --signing-provider-sha256 "$QINAO_WAVE_BUNDLE_REVIEW_SIGNING_PROVIDER_SHA256" \
  --output "$QINAO_CURRENT_WAVE_BUNDLE"
```

The external verifier rederives every referenced blob and base before asking
the provider to sign. A V1 output bundle embeds neither its own blob nor its
candidate tree. A V2 output bundle embeds no reference to its own bytes, path,
digest, report, or receipt, but its closed production requirement does bind
the already prepared candidate commit/tree and refs. `wave-bundle-reviewer`
cannot sign an admission receipt, and
`wave-admission-signer` cannot sign a bundle.

External prerequisite paths are never repository paths or candidate bytes.
They must be pairwise-distinct, outside the worktree, regular files with mode
`0600`, and already exist. Before accepting their digests, every one of the
five commands opens the bytes itself and validates the declared schema,
signature, trusted role, repository identity, outcome, and schema-specific
linkage. For a fresh nonterminal prerequisite it also proves unexpired
eligibility at the downstream claim's trusted `authorizationEffectiveAt`; an
already-open downstream claim instead recovers only its frozen bytes under the
expiry rule above. The sole post-migration K4 exception is not “ignore
expiry": all five consumers must prove the exact blob was timely admitted by
the migration terminal, while the W5 controller additionally performs the
fresh live-profile revalidation defined above before opening its claim. A
second specialized historical-use rule applies only to certification's exact
runtime chain: the Apple receipt must bind the generation it timely consumed,
and certification reopens that identical chain under the two-consumer rule
above. A digest claim copied into a bundle is not proof.
For `runtime-receipt-chain`, schema-specific linkage means independently
verifying the `runtime-chain-signer` signature, receipts 01 through 06 in
ordinal order, every receipt's predecessor/installed-commit-and-tree
continuity, and the chain's expected head commit/tree. The chain embeds all six complete canonical signed
`QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV2` objects plus the digest of each canonical object;
a digest-only entry or an external path hidden inside the chain is invalid.
Thus every consumer can reverify all six admission signatures from the one
external chain input. The repository runner and external verifier each
perform this validation; neither trusts the other's report.

The V1 shapes remain valid only for Task 1's historical W0 transition. The
following six replacements are the complete V2 mapping owned by this plan;
the controlled documents adopt it and the ignored Amendment-2 view is
regenerated from them, never used as a circular normative source:

- `QinaoWaveCategoryEvidenceV2` has exactly the V1 top-level member set and
  constraints with only its `schema` literal and `reviewedRows` element shape
  changed. `create|extension|adapter` rows are closed
  `AuthorityCategoryRowV2` values with exactly `{path,sourceKind,symbol,
  entityDigest,contentBinding,change,ownerID,classification,authorityClaims,
  ownerBasis}`. `fixture` rows are closed `FixtureCategoryRowV2` values with
  exactly `{path,sourceKind:"fixtureFile",symbol:"@file",entityDigest,
  contentBinding,change,ownerID,proofTask,ownerBasis}`. The existing
  `reviewedRowsRoot` hashes the sorted complete V2 rows.
- `QinaoWaveBundleV2` has exactly the V1 top-level member set plus
  `fixtureProofRows`, `protectedCommandPolicy`, and
  `protectedValidationRequirement`, with `schema` replaced by the V2
  literal. `fixtureProofRows` is the exact current-slice Ledger fixture-proof
  set and is bijective with the internal fixture delta.
  `protectedCommandPolicy` is exactly `{authorizingOwnerLedgerBlobDigest,
  targetOwnerLedgerBlobDigest,policyRoot}` and both Ledger-opened nested
  policies must equal it. `protectedValidationRequirement` is the closed
  static `productionWave` object frozen in Task 1; the separate
  Ledger-migration requirement and the bundle-free Ordinary fixture route are
  never embedded in a Wave bundle.
- `QinaoWaveCandidateReportV2` has exactly the V1 member set plus
  `fixtureProof:{root,count}`, the complete independently rederived
  `protectedCommandPolicy`, and the static `protectedCandidateObservation`,
  with only
  the schema literal replaced. The proof root is
  `SHA256(RFC8785(sorted bundle.fixtureProofRows))`; its count is exact.
- `QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV2` has exactly the V1 member set plus the same
  independently rederived `fixtureProof:{root,count}`, complete policy
  binding and static `protectedCandidateObservation`, plus the controller-only
  `protectedValidationObservation` and closed `targetRefInstallation` terminal
  defined below, with only the schema literal replaced. It never embeds the
  unsigned report.
- `QinaoW6RuntimeReceiptChainV2` has exactly the V1 chain member set and
  continuity/signature rules with only its schema literal replaced; every
  `entries[].receipt` is one complete `QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV2` and every
  expected embedded receipt discriminator is V2.
- `QinaoAdmissionCanonicalVectorSetV2` has exactly the V1 vector-set member
  set with its schema literal replaced; every category/bundle/report/receipt/
  runtime-chain vector uses only the closed V2 shapes above. It additionally
  contains Ledger-migration, entity-policy, fixture-proof, specialized K4,
  offline-profile, artifact-envelope-V2, protected-candidate, version-bridge,
  target-ref/operation-instance recovery, prepared-commit metadata,
  static pre-controller Report versus controller-only validation observation
  and post-CAS receipt installation terminal,
  protected-review envelope, and same-tree/different-commit mutations. Task 1 independently reviews,
  admits, and freezes the V2 vector before migration; Task 2 only deletes the
  V1 vector while reopening the exact unchanged V2 bytes.

For the scheduled K4 slice only, the V2 bundle's specialized external
requirement row has exactly `{name,schema,blobDigest,requiredOutcome,
requiredProfileDigest,requiredApprovedDesignBlob}`. Its Report/Receipt
verified row adds exactly `{verifiedOutcome,verifiedProfileDigest,
verifiedApprovedDesignBlob}`. Literals are
`name == "k4-ios27-platform-spike"`,
`schema == "QinaoK4IOS27PlatformSpikeV1"`, and
`requiredOutcome == "supportedExactProfile"`. Here `requiredOutcome` is the
Wave-requirement field and `verifiedOutcome` is its verification projection;
both must equal the reopened evidence object's canonical
`status == "supportedExactProfile"`. They do not imply an `outcome` member in
the K4 evidence schema. Every other V2 external
prerequisite retains the generic V1 row shape. No implementation-selected,
extra, optional/defaulted, or cross-version member is permitted. The
containing Wave bundle is V2; the independently admitted K4 evidence wire
remains its sole declared V1 schema and is never relabelled as a nonexistent
K4 V2 object. W5 candidate base/tree and production diff are already bound by
the Wave V2 requirement/report; they are not fictitious fields copied into a
platform-spike evidence schema.

creates no production operation-instance/claim, and has no target/prepared
ref, installation, CAS, signer, or receipt path. Production requires
`waveAdmission` and a controller-minted trusted-live challenge only after the
static bundle/report match.

Every static requirement/candidate-observation pair maps by exact bytes and
every root is recomputed. The controller-only observation must in turn match
that static pair and independently prove the challenge/run/Result/retention/
finalization facts; there is no prefix inference, omitted execution-derived
proof, or caller-made projection.

The one pure projection is exact:

```text
project_static_candidate(receipt.protectedValidationObservation)
  == receipt.protectedCandidateObservation
  == report.protectedCandidateObservation
  == map_required_to_observed(bundle.protectedValidationRequirement)

receipt.protectedValidationObservation.requiredEvidenceRetentionNotBefore
  == receipt.protectedValidationObservation.challengeExpiresAt
     + receipt.protectedCandidateObservation.evidenceRetentionDurationSeconds
```

The duration is exactly `259200`; overflow, mismatched policy roots, any
dynamic field in the static objects, or a projection mismatch fails before
target-ref CAS.

The controller creates or resumes its one operation claim only after both the
signed static bundle and unsigned static Candidate Report match. It then mints
the live challenge and finalizes the production validation observation before
target-ref installation. Candidate Report V2 can therefore claim neither
dynamic validation nor a CAS result. Only `QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV2`
carries that controller observation and adds this closed
`targetRefInstallation` terminal:

```text
{
  operationInstanceKey,
  targetRefName, preparedRefName,
  refExpectedOldOID, refInstalledOID, refCASResultRoot,
  installedCommit, installedTree, reopenedOwnerLedgerBlobDigest,
  preparedRefDisposition, preparedRefDeleteCASResultRoot,
  controllerTransactionID, installedAt, state, outcome
}
```

Its literals and equalities are
`refExpectedOldOID == baseCommit`,
`refInstalledOID == installedCommit == candidateCommit`,
`installedTree == candidateTree`,
`reopenedOwnerLedgerBlobDigest == targetOwnerLedgerBlobDigest`,
`preparedRefDisposition == "deleted"`, `state == "installed"`, and
`outcome == "passed"`; both CAS result roots are nonempty domain-separated
roots over their exact expected/current/new OIDs and controller transaction.
The signed receipt is ineligible until the controller
has re-opened the installed full target ref/tree/Ledger and confirmed the
prepared ref no longer exists. That retirement is itself compare-and-delete
from the exact candidate OID after the installed reopen; a missing/moved ref
outside a matching resumed claim or any different OID blocks the terminal.

For a production V2 Wave,
`requiredOperationInstanceKey == operationInstanceKey` and equals:

```text
lowerHex(SHA256(
  ASCII("QINAO-WAVE-V2-INSTANCE-V1") || 0x00 ||
  RFC8785([
    repositoryIdentity, operationID, admissionKind, wave, waveSliceID,
    sequenceOrdinal, targetRefName, preparedRefName,
    baseCommit, baseTree, candidateCommit, candidateTree,
    requiredPredecessorReceiptBlob, approvedDesignBlob,
    productionDiffRoot, pathList.root,
    authorizingOwnerLedgerBlobDigest, targetOwnerLedgerBlobDigest,
    policyRoot, requiredToolRowsRoot
  ])
))
```

The key intentionally excludes every authorization root created only after
the controller claim begins, every root that covers the requirement or key
itself, plus bundle/report/receipt bytes, their paths, challenge, signature
nonce, process identity, retry count, and timestamps, so it cannot form a
self-hash edge or fork on retry. Only after independently rederiving both the
signed static bundle and static Candidate Report does the existing external
controller create/resume the claim. Its `bundleVerified` transition atomically
stores the complete bundle bytes/digest/root and static-report digest as
immutable claim data under that key; only then may it issue a challenge. A
different bundle/report for the same key is corruption, not a second
operation.

The existing controller's single durable claim advances monotonically through
exactly `prepared -> bundleVerified -> validationFinalized -> refAdvanced ->
candidateReopened -> preparedRefRetired -> terminalPersisted ->
receiptPublished`. The only authority-changing effect is a compare-and-swap
of the bound full target ref from `baseCommit` to `candidateCommit`. A signer
request is forbidden before `candidateReopened` and `preparedRefRetired`; a
terminal receipt is forbidden before that signature and the matching bytes
are durably persisted. Report generation and bundle review never move a ref.
The repository runner never moves or deletes either ref.
Here `terminalPersisted` means the one canonical signed receipt is durable in
the protected evidence transaction; `receiptPublished` means those identical
bytes have been exclusively materialized at the caller's external receipt
path. Publication never creates or re-signs another receipt.

A protected-validation denial before `refAdvanced` follows the separate closed
sequence `validationDenied -> failedEvidencePersisted -> preparedRefRetired ->
nonAdmissionTerminalPersisted`. It persists the failed Result/finalization
under the same operation key, compare-and-deletes only that claim's exact
prepared ref, leaves the target ref at `baseCommit`, and emits no Wave
admission receipt. A corrected candidate has a different candidate
tree/commit, prepared ref, and operation key and starts only after the failed
claim is terminal. Failure cleanup cannot move the target ref or turn denial
into admission.

Unknown outcomes use this closed recovery matrix:

```text
target == base + no claim
  start the one operation
target == base + matching nonterminal claim before refAdvanced
  resume the same claim; reuse commit, bundle, challenge, and run
target == candidate + matching nonterminal claim
  do not CAS again; reopen candidate and continue the same claim
target == candidate + matching terminal/receiptPublished claim
  return the byte-identical persisted receipt; never sign again
target == base + matching failed nonterminal + prepared == candidate
  resume only that claim's exact compare-delete; never rerun validation,
  resign the bundle, CAS the target, or emit an admission receipt
target == base + matching failed nonterminal + prepared absent
  persist the same non-admission terminal from existing failed evidence;
  never rerun validation or emit an admission receipt
target == base + matching failed non-admission terminal + prepared absent
  replay the byte-identical denial/finalization disposition; never rerun,
  resign, CAS the target, or emit an admission receipt
any matching failed state + prepared == other
  quarantine as failed-claim cleanup corruption
target == other
  quarantine as target drift
target == base + installed terminal
  quarantine as impossible rollback/corruption
target == candidate + no matching claim
  quarantine as an unowned installed state
matching claim + different prepared commit, bundle, predecessor, or policy
  quarantine as operation-identity corruption
```

On an unknown CAS, persistence, or signing result, recovery first queries the
target ref, durable claim, protected evidence transaction, and scoped signer
request. It never blindly repeats CAS, changes nonce/output path, creates a
new commit, or asks for a second signature. Loss of a local receipt cache may
only restore the exact canonical bytes already held by the terminal evidence
transaction. Once `receiptPublished` is verified, the coordinator advances
the external previous-receipt pointer to those bytes; it cannot advance on a
report, ref movement alone, or a digest-only record.

```text
  nativeTerminalReceipt, nativeTerminalStoredSHA256, nativeTerminalRoot,
  sharedB0BindingRoot, commandCoverageRoot,
  pythonExecutionContractRoot, nativeExecutionContractRoot,
  executionContractEqualityRoot,
  pythonSequenceRoot, nativeSequenceRoot, sequenceEqualityRoot,
  pythonDerivationComparisonRoot, nativeDerivationComparisonRoot,
  derivationEqualityRoot,
  pythonAssertionPlanRoot, nativeAssertionPlanRoot, assertionPlanEqualityRoot,
  pythonAssertionResultRoot, nativeAssertionResultRoot,
  assertionResultEqualityRoot, distinctRunIdentityProofRoot,
  pythonRetentionLeaseRoot, nativeRetentionLeaseRoot,
  requiredEvidenceRetentionNotBefore,
  state, outcome, finalizedAt,
  signerID, signerRole, signatureAlgorithm, signature, pairRoot
}
```

The pair embeds both complete terminal receipts, requires distinct
surface/challenge/run/scratch identities, byte-identical governed contracts
and sequences, equal successful derivations/assertions, and a retention
horizon equal to the later surface requirement. Eligible literals are
`state == "finalizedReadOnly"` and `outcome == "passed"`. All three envelopes
use RFC-8785-plus-LF stored bytes and domain-separated roots; the incumbent
provider exposes only these exact schema-scoped signing operations. This is a
new evidence schema under the existing controller, not a new signer,
controller, store, owner, operation, or admission authority.

Across both Wave versions, the bundle binds `repositoryIdentity`,
`waveSliceID`, `sequenceOrdinal`, `requiredPredecessorReceiptBlob`,
`requiredPredecessorCandidateTree`, evidence-prerequisite blobs/statuses,
signer/role, issue/expiry, nonce, signature algorithm, and signature. The
receipt binds the verified bundle/selection/trust-root/external-verifier/
repository-runner tool blobs, base commit/tree, candidate tree, production
diff root, path-list root, category roots/counts, evidence- and external-
prerequisite normalized names/schema/digests/statuses, slice/ordinal,
previous receipt, outcome, signer/role, time, nonce, and signature. Bundles
require the `wave-bundle-reviewer` role; receipts require
`wave-admission-signer`. Every version uses the same RFC 8785 + SHA-256 +
Ed25519 convention as Task 0, while schema/key scopes prevent cross-version
substitution. V2 additionally binds the exact candidate commit, target/
prepared refs, operation-instance key, and terminal installation observation;
those members are not retrofitted into historical V1.

The phase-indexed chain is exact:

```text
signed root admission receipt.selectedTree
-> optional signed design-edge candidateTree
-> zero or more historical Wave V1 receipts through Task 1/W0
-> QinaoLedgerV2MigrationTerminalReceiptV1
   .predecessorCommit^{tree} == .predecessorTree
   .predecessorTree == final verified V1 predecessor candidateTree
   .candidateCommit/tree == installed Ledger-V2 migration commit/tree
-> first Wave V2 bundle baseCommit/tree
   == migration terminal candidateCommit/tree
-> zero or more Wave V2 receipts
   .targetRefInstallation.installedCommit/tree
   == protected target-ref commit/tree
   == next Wave V2 bundle baseCommit/tree
```

The root admission receipt anchors only the root; it is not reused as the
immediate predecessor of every later wave. Every bundle/receipt signature,
trusted role, repository, expiry, nonce, previous receipt, base tree,
candidate commit/tree where present, path-list blob, category blob, evidence
prerequisite, and slice ordinal is verified. Historical V1 accepts its commit
only after `HEAD^{tree}` equals the admitted tree. V2 accepts installation only
when the bound full target ref equals the terminal's exact installed commit and
reopens to the exact admitted tree; tree equality alone never suffices.

The post-migration predecessor union is phase constrained. The migration
terminal receipt is the only legal bridge from the historical V1 chain to the
first V2 Wave and may occur exactly once. Its protected operation
authorization reopens the immediate V1 predecessor receipt and full chain,
while `predecessorRootReceiptDigest` anchors the original root; a root digest
alone is insufficient. The first V2 bundle reopens the complete migration
terminal receipt and requires its candidate commit/tree and installed Ledger
blob/root to equal the bundle base. Thereafter only a complete
`QinaoWaveAdmissionReceiptV2` may be the immediate Wave predecessor. A Wave V1
receipt, ordinary report, migration Result without terminal receipt,
same-tree/different-commit object, digest-only reference, second migration
terminal, or relabelled design/root receipt can never bridge the versions.

This avoids an impossible hash cycle. Historical V1 W0 may commit its reviewed
bundle because that schema does not bind the containing candidate identity.
For V2, committed manifests, dispositions, and path lists bind exact intended
path/blob/diff roots but never embed their containing candidate commit/tree;
the complete unsigned/signed bundle is external and may therefore bind that
already prepared identity. The repository runner computes the unsigned
candidate report from the staged index and prepared commit; the external
verifier independently recomputes it and the existing controller performs the
installation/signature sequence above. The repository runner then verifies
but cannot prepare authority, sign, move a target ref, or admit. V2 bundles,
reports, receipts, and final receipt chains are never staged into the tree
they describe or attest. The next bundle binds the prior external receipt
blob/digest and its installed commit/tree.

For every V2 slice, the execution coordinator requires the unsigned-bundle,
reviewed-bundle, unsigned-report, current-receipt, and previous-receipt paths
to be outside the repository, mode `0600`, regular, non-symlink,
descriptor-stable-open, and pairwise distinct by path and inode. Historical
Task-1/W0 V1 keeps the reviewed bundle at the fixed repository tree path
`qinao-dual-space-w0-gates-wave-bundle.json`, but the reviewer's output path is
external. Its canonical unsigned preimage passes a real
`wave-bundle-reviewer` operation, then the preparation broker byte-exactly
materializes those reviewed bytes at the fixed tree path before the final
candidate tree. Its unsigned report plus current/previous receipt paths obey
the same external-file rules. No signer or reviewer writes a repository path.

Fresh outputs use exclusive creation plus file-and-parent-directory fsync;
an existing exact output is a recovery input, not a restart blocker. After
interruption, an existing output is never overwritten or treated as a new
attempt: the coordinator queries the applicable signing/operation claim,
stable-opens the existing bytes,
and requires exact schema, bundle, predecessor, candidate commit/tree, refs,
operation-instance/authorization roots, challenge/run identity, nonce, and
signature equality. A matching V1 receipt resumes at verification and its
historical local commit step; a matching V2 receipt resumes at
installed-ref/receipt verification only. A matching nonterminal claim resumes
or reconciles that claim; any mismatch is quarantined. It never requests a
second signature merely because a process or task ended. Every new V2 slice
receives fresh external artifact paths. Only after the V2 target-ref
commit/tree, reopened Ledger, installation terminal, and receipt bytes all
verify may it promote `QINAO_CURRENT_ADMISSION_RECEIPT` to the next slice's
`QINAO_PREVIOUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT`; cross-slice reuse or overwrite fails. The
V1 in-tree-bundle layout applies only through Task 1/W0; external signer
outputs are mandatory for every version and slice.

  Every authoritative fenced execution block is fail-fast: the protected
  controller executes its logical commands in order and terminates the wave on
  the first nonzero status. A later command, receipt, commit or successful
  shell exit can never mask an earlier failure. Every non-empty Swift/Xcode
  runner command invokes the admitted absolute protected-Python projection as
  its first argv and the runner path as its second argv. Shell control
  operators, conditional/loop/function/alias wrappers, command substitution,
  redirection, and PATH/Python-environment reassignment are forbidden in or
  around a required runner. Standalone shell-flow or error-state builtins and
  wrappers—`exit`, `return`, `set`, `trap`, `true`, `false`, `:`, `eval`,
  `source`, `.`, `exec`, `builtin`, and `command`—are likewise forbidden in
  such a fenced block; none can mask, replace or reinterpret a logical command.
  The controller consumes the already-expanded argv rather than evaluating a
  free-form shell string.

  `run_nonempty_xcode_test.py` is a separate iOS runner. It accepts exactly one
  mutually exclusive source selector: either an exact Swift-package directory
  through `--package-path`, or an exact `.xcodeproj` bundle through

  selectors, a workspace, a symlinked/escaped project, a missing/non-regular
  `project.pbxproj`, and every unknown or abbreviated selector. Both modes

  absolute repository-external DerivedData and result-bundle roots, and exactly
  one singleton `--require-target`. It also accepts repeatable exact
  `--require-suite Target/Suite` and
  `--require-test Target/Suite/testName` selectors. When either is present the
  set must be nonempty, duplicate-free and closed: every test belongs to one
  required suite and the singleton target, every suite owns at least one test,
  and the runner derives only the corresponding exact `-only-testing:` argv.
  Structured discovery/execution must equal those selectors bidirectionally;
  an extra, missing, renamed, skipped or expected-failure case fails. With no
  suite/test selector, the whole singleton target remains the closed selection.
  Package mode derives only
  `xcodebuild -packagePath`; project mode derives only `xcodebuild -project`

  `ordinary.fixture-report`; it has no OIDC token, secret, production trust
  root, real candidate input, upload, signer, admission receipt, or promotion
  path. `.github/workflows/qinao-wave-admission.yml` prepares and verifies
  protected inputs under the `qinao-admission` environment, but remains
  fail-closed at Phase C until Task 2 installs the exact

  the required terminal, retention, and pair receipts. Neither workflow
  accepts `risk_tier`, `admission_kind`, or `operation_id` from a caller.

`QinaoK4IOS27PlatformSpikeV1` is a signed evidence schema, not an owner. Its
canonical fields are: schema/repository/design identities; Xcode/SDK/OS build;
signed physical-device profile digest; exact framework/API and availability;
target/extension/process model; signing and entitlement inventory; SQLite
open/WAL/file-protection constraints; transport/XPC feasibility; launch,
interruption, termination, reconnect, and key-access observations; test/result
bundle digests; exact supported profile digest; status
`supportedExactProfile|disabledMissingTarget|disabledMissingEntitlement|
disabledMissingDeviceProof`; signer/role; issue/expiry; nonce; signature.
It uses the common RFC 8785/Ed25519 envelope. Transition 04 may admit it only
under an unexpired signing/migration claim. W5's bundle must bind the exact
migration-admitted blob, `supportedExactProfile`, profile digest, and valid
historical signature; the W5 controller separately proves the live profile is
still byte-identical/current before its claim. The wave runner mutation-tests
evidence that was stale before migration claim, not migration-admitted,
disabled, wrong-profile, unsigned, wrong-device, or live-profile-divergent.

### Closed post-migration V2 Wave slice registry

Task 2 installs exactly these fourteen production operation rows in the sole
protected command policy. In every row, `operationID == waveSliceID`,
`admissionKind == "waveAdmission"`, controller is the existing
`wave-admission-controller`, target ref and base commit/tree are inherited
from the immediate predecessor terminal/receipt named in the table, and
prepared ref is the exact hash-derived ref defined by the preparation CLI.
No free-text operation/slice/ref mapping, extra macro slice, caller-selected
target/base, or caller-selected ordinal is legal.

Managed transition 17 is deliberately outside those fourteen Wave rows. The
sole protected policy contains exactly one non-Wave runtime-chain operation
binding, byte-for-byte:

```text
operationID = "w6.runtime-receipt-chain"
admissionKind = "runtimeChainPublication"
waveSliceID = ""
entrypointID = "external-admission-verifier"
waveAdmissionEligible = false
stateMutationEligible = false
```

That binding permits only the incumbent verifier's closed
`sign-runtime-chain` / `verify-runtime-chain` transaction and its recoverable
claim/publication records after W6 receipt 06 is verified. It cannot prepare a
Wave candidate, consume category evidence, move a Git ref, mutate Ledger or
runtime state, act as a Wave predecessor receipt, or substitute its signed
chain for W6 receipt 06. An empty `waveSliceID` is mandatory precisely because
this is publication of the separately governed six-receipt chain, not a Wave
slice; assigning `waveAdmission`, Wave eligibility, state-mutation eligibility,
or a nonempty slice ID is a policy-shape failure.

The managed coordinator sets W1's predecessor path to
`$QINAO_LEDGER_V2_MIGRATION_TERMINAL_RECEIPT`. After each V2 operation reaches
`receiptPublished` and repository verification succeeds, it atomically
advances `$QINAO_PREVIOUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT` to those same canonical receipt
bytes; W2 through W6 may consume that pointer only after reopening the exact
predecessor named by this registry. A report, local file rename, prepared ref,
target-ref movement without a terminal, or digest-only cache cannot advance
the pointer. For every row the coordinator derives
`$QINAO_CURRENT_TARGET_REF` from that verified predecessor and reopens the
live ref into `$QINAO_CURRENT_BASE_COMMIT`/`$QINAO_CURRENT_BASE_TREE`; the
preparation utility requires those live values to equal the predecessor's
installed commit/tree. The matching command-line values are redundant
equality witnesses, never operator or model choices.

Every registry row also owns exactly four current category-evidence import
paths. If its prefix is `P`, those paths are exactly
`docs/superpowers/evidence/P-{create,extension,adapter,fixture}-category-evidence-v2.json`.
All four paths occur exactly once in that row's candidate path list and in the
candidate Ledger admission registry. There are therefore exactly 56 V2
category-evidence paths: no W0 reuse, inferred filename, optional fifth path,
or future plan naming decision exists. The evidence object's derived
`present|notApplicable` status is independent of the filename.
The Task-2 Ledger registry freezes only
`{waveSliceID,sequenceOrdinal,category,schema,fixedRepositoryPath,ownerBasis}`
for each future evidence row. It never stores a future category blob digest,
signature, evidence root, candidate tree/commit, or ref. `draft-bundle` opens
the actual signed blob from the current candidate tree at that fixed path and
binds its digest after category import. This one-way path template prevents a
Ledger-to-category-to-candidate self-hash cycle.

The Task-2 Ledger migration freezes W1's Artifact-Mesh proof as one closed
subgraph of the sole `QinaoProtectedCommandPolicyV1`. That same object, rather
than a second dispatcher manifest or Store, also freezes the execution edge
for every managed transition 05-19. Fourteen of those bindings are the Wave
rows in the closed post-migration registry and have
`admissionKind == "waveAdmission"`, `waveSliceID == operationID`,
`entrypointID == "wave-admission-controller"`,
`waveAdmissionEligible == true`, and `stateMutationEligible == true`.
Transition 17 is the one separately frozen non-Wave runtime-chain binding
defined at the head of that registry; it is never relabelled as a
fifteenth Wave. The W1 operation binding is byte-exact:

```text
operationID = "w1.artifact-mesh-contract-freeze"
admissionKind = "waveAdmission"
waveSliceID = "w1.artifact-mesh-contract-freeze"
entrypointID = "wave-admission-controller"
waveAdmissionEligible = true
stateMutationEligible = true
```

The protected-policy row shapes are exact and include the current
`stateMutationEligible` binding member:

```text
toolRows[] = {
  toolID, sourceKind, path, gitBlobOID, mode, byteLength, sha256
}

commandRows[] = {

  authorizedOperationIDs, ordinaryEligible, descendantProfileID,
  timeoutMilliseconds, cpuSeconds, maxSampledPhysicalFootprint,
  maxStdoutBytes, maxStderrBytes, resultKind, resultAuthority,

  expectedExternalInputIDs, expectedAssertionIDs
}

}

assertionRows[] = {

  mutationLocator, mutationDigest, expectedOutcome, expectedReasonCode
}
```

The containing policy is constructible rather than an implicit collection of
those four arrays. Its top-level object has exactly:

```text
{
  schema:"QinaoProtectedCommandPolicyV1",
  policyID:"qinao.protected-command-policy.v1",
  policyVersion:1,
  operationBindings[], evidenceRetentionPolicyRows[],
  descendantProfiles[], executableRows[], invocationTemplates[],
  toolRows[], commandRows[], externalInputRequirements[], assertionRows[],
  operationCoverageRows[], managedTransitionEndpointRows[],
  operationBindingsRoot, evidenceRetentionPolicyRowsRoot,
  descendantProfilesRoot, executableRowsRoot, invocationTemplatesRoot,
  toolRowsRoot, commandRowsRoot, externalInputRequirementRowsRoot,
  assertionRowsRoot, operationCoverageRowsRoot,
  managedTransitionEndpointRowsRoot
}

operationBindings[] = {
  operationID, admissionKind, waveSliceID, entrypointID,
  waveAdmissionEligible, stateMutationEligible
}

evidenceRetentionPolicyRows[] = {
  policyID, durationSeconds, startEvent, custodyClass,
  cleanupReceiptRequired
}

descendantProfiles[] = {

}

environmentRows[] = { name, valueKind, literalValue, externalInputID }
mountRows[] = {

}
fileDescriptorRows[] = { descriptor, disposition, capabilityKind }

executableRows[] = {

}

}

  externalInputRequirementRowsRoot, toolRowsRoot, descendantProfilesRoot,
  executableRowsRoot, invocationTemplatesRoot,
  managedTransitionEndpointRowIDs, managedTransitionEndpointRowsRoot
}

managedTransitionEndpointRows[] = {
  endpointRowID, transitionID, operationID, action, toolID, executableID,
  invocationTemplateID, endpointKind, argvTemplate,
  allowedPlaceholderNames, resultSchema
}
```

`managedTransitionEndpointRows[]` contains exactly 45 rows: exactly three rows
for each transition ID 05 through 19 and no other transition. Their IDs are
exactly
`managed.<transitionID>.<queryExisting|invokeOnce|verifyExisting>`, their
`operationID` equals the closed nineteen-transition registry row, and
`resultSchema == "QinaoManagedTransitionObservationV1"`. For each managed
operation, its `operationCoverageRows[]` member names those exact three sorted
endpoint-row IDs and repeats the domain-separated root of that three-row
canonical subset. The top-level `managedTransitionEndpointRowsRoot` covers the
complete canonically ID-sorted 45-row array.

This does not evict the same policy's existing Ordinary or protected-read-only
operation bindings. Every nonmanaged coverage row still carries the two new
members, but `managedTransitionEndpointRowIDs == []` and
`managedTransitionEndpointRowsRoot` equals the domain-separated root of the
empty array. The coordinator preserves and root-validates those rows as policy
data but derives no transition contract or executable binding from them. A
nonmanaged row that names any of the 45 managed endpoints, or a managed row
missing one of its three, fails closed.

Every endpoint row resolves its `toolID -> executableID ->
invocationTemplateID` chain through this same policy. The executable admits
that template; at least one coverage-bound descendant profile admits both;
the operation coverage names the tool, executable, template, and profile; and
both `permitsShell` and `permitsPATHLookup` are false. A generic shell,
generic-command, private-key, or signing-provider endpoint kind is never a
direct managed action. Explicit sharing of an immutable execution tool or
profile across managed operations is legal only when every referencing
coverage row names it; an endpoint row itself belongs to exactly one managed
operation and cannot be aliased.

`argvTemplate` is a nonempty string-token array accepted by the coordinator's
closed placeholder validator, and `allowedPlaceholderNames` is the exact
sorted set rederived from those tokens. All three actions bind transition,
operation, source-selection, trust-root, and review-source identity.
`queryExisting` must not contain `expectedState`,
`expectedObservationRoot`, or `claimKey`; `invokeOnce` and `verifyExisting`
must contain all three so an effect or verification remains bound to the same
observed durable claim. An unknown placeholder, environment expansion, shell
syntax, missing reference, extra row, reordered row, root mismatch, or dynamic
value on `queryExisting` blocks migration or replay.

Every array is ordered by its primary `*ID` as RFC-8785 strings; every root is
the domain-separated SHA-256 of that canonical array. `parentProfileID` is
JSON null for all W1 profiles. An omitted/extra/defaulted member, unreferenced
row, root mismatch, cycle, unknown ID or many-to-one alias fails migration.

All template rows have `permitsShell=false` and `permitsPATHLookup=false`.

root and the closed read-only object/ref queries required by the owning script;
it rejects configuration injection, hooks, signing, PATH lookup and an argv
not derived by that script. `swift-package` permits only the literal package path and `test`
subcommand. No environment expansion, response file, glob, working-directory
escape, `-c`, `-m` outside the one frozen module, or argument beginning with
an unrecognized option is legal.

Negative mutations live in the independently rooted checker/wrapper meta-test
corpora and use distinct `negativeControl` rows there; a positive row may
never smuggle a mutation locator. No `diagnostic` result can satisfy a
protected assertion.

The W1 `operationCoverageRows` member names the operation binding above,

required by the row shape and equality-checks them to the top-level roots; it

The W1 proof subgraph is valid only when reverse traversal from every W1 proof

rejected. The remaining fourteen coverage rows carry their own exact three
managed endpoint rows and closed execution references without becoming a

Task 2 constructs every top-level array in canonical row-ID order, rejects
duplicates, and requires exact set equality in both directions against the
tables above. It recomputes every declared root; the operation coverage row
contains the exact unions and those same roots, plus the exact per-operation
three-row endpoint subset/root. Tests delete, add, rename, retarget and reorder
every row class—including any of the 45 managed endpoint rows—and verify both

requirement roots are static
in the bundle; the controller alone derives the dynamic observation and stores
it only in the one W1 V2 terminal receipt. A second Task-0 receipt, handoff,

For each row, `$QINAO_UNSIGNED_WAVE_BUNDLE`,
`$QINAO_CURRENT_WAVE_BUNDLE`, `$QINAO_UNSIGNED_ADMISSION_REPORT`, and
`$QINAO_CURRENT_ADMISSION_RECEIPT` are fresh external paths satisfying the

directories are external and distinct from those four files. The candidate
path list names every and only staged Git path and rejects every external
artifact. The fresh-path dependency order is: draft four category preimages;
independently review/sign them externally; byte-exact import all four inert
copies; stage/write the candidate tree; prepare the deterministic commit/ref;
